concepts.claim: When redundancy cannot meet the latency budget the service descends a ladder validated before the incident (model fallback, feature fallback, load shedding, admission control) with hysteresis and monitoring of the quality it trades.

concepts.label: Fault injection at the decision level
concepts.claim: A recovery path is trustworthy only for the fault model it has been exercised against, so tests inject faults where recovery decisions are made and assert the invariant each decision depends on.

concepts.label: Fault-tolerance investment criterion
concepts.claim: A protection is worth buying while it removes more expected failure cost than it adds, so the same hot spare that pays for itself beside a 10,000-GPU job is waste beside an 8-GPU one.

concepts.label: Observability for one distributed job
concepts.claim: Metrics, logs, and traces joined on shared identifiers localize a failure in one job or service, and a training-loss signature or serving symptom becomes evidence only when it maps to a first recovery action.

concepts.label: Scheduler as allocation control plane
concepts.claim: A cluster scheduler loses direct observation, atomic effect, and binary failure, so it separates admission, placement, and reconciliation, and reusing a suspect node's accelerators requires versioned allocations, leases, and fencing.

concepts.label: Gang scheduling
concepts.claim: A rigid synchronous job makes no progress below its minimum gang, so partial allocation can deadlock two jobs at full cost, and atomic all-or-nothing allocation removes hold-and-wait but needs reservation, safe backfill, and holistic preemption.

concepts.label: Feasibility before fairness
concepts.claim: A fair share of accelerators a job cannot run on delivers nothing, so the scheduler first filters feasible bundles (every resource dimension, gang atomicity, topology, memory) and only then applies dominant-resource fairness, while multi-dimensional packing strands capacity.

concepts.label: Scheduling objectives and matched signals
concepts.claim: Throughput, latency, fairness, and cost pull allocation apart, so fairness is measured as slowdown, queue delay grows with job-size variability (M/G/1), and an ML-aware policy earns its cost only when its signal matches the objective.

concepts.label: Topology-aware placement
concepts.claim: Equal-size allocations deliver different throughput because bandwidth steps down from NVLink to leaf to spine, so placement minimizes a locality cost over the job's actual traffic, judged by completion time including the wait for a compact placement.

concepts.label: Elastic scheduling contract
concepts.claim: Elasticity replaces keep-or-kill with a declared size range, valid increments, a measured transition cost, and a scaling-efficiency curve, and each resize must be amortized over the run and judged by time to target quality.

concepts.label: Interruption economics
concepts.claim: Every preemption pays discarded work since the last durable checkpoint plus reload and warmup, one admission can cascade into many evictions, and spot capacity is cheap only by effective cost after checkpoint overhead, restart, and replay.

concepts.label: Utilization tiers
concepts.claim: Utilization is worth money at fleet scale, but an unlabeled percentage conflates the allocated tier (complete allocations only), the active tier, and the productive tier (normalized to the job's fault-free step rate), and a full queue beside idle accelerators is usually a policy-infrastructure mismatch rather than an algorithm defect.

concepts.label: Batch versus declarative orchestration
concepts.claim: Slurm's imperative batch allocation and Kubernetes' level-triggered reconciliation are different contracts for which lifecycle the platform manages, chosen by workload semantics, and a hybrid works only when exactly one layer owns each placement.

concepts.label: Quota guarantees bounded by reclaim
concepts.claim: Hierarchical quotas separate a team's guarantee from its maximum and borrowing idle guarantees lifts utilization, but concurrently honored guarantees must fit the capacity the platform can reclaim in time, and a noisy neighbor, one tenant whose consumption of a shared resource slows the others, is what isolation and reclaim contracts must bound.

concepts.label: Serving envelope and accelerator sharing
concepts.claim: The orchestrator's serving unit is a ready replica sized by measured capacity at a latency target, colocation trades density against interference along an isolation spectrum (time-slicing, MPS, MIG, exclusive), and moving devices between training and serving is safe only on forecast.

concepts.label: Waiting time versus utilization
concepts.claim: Mean queue wait is a load factor rho/(1-rho) times a variability factor (1+C_s^2)/2, so waiting time bends sharply upward as offered load nears capacity, and a mixed ML queue whose job durations vary widely pays several times more wait at the same utilization than a uniform one.

concepts.label: ML goodput
concepts.claim: Useful fleet output is capacity times scheduling, runtime, and program goodput, each counted on one accounting boundary so every lost hour is charged to exactly one factor.

concepts.label: Reproducible measurement contract
concepts.claim: A goodput or optimization claim is valid only against a fixed contract that names the factor and window measured along with the workload and quality gate, system state, timing boundary, load-generation mode, and repeated trials with tails, so cold-start and warmed trials are reported apart.

concepts.label: Fleet profiling by hierarchy and sampling
concepts.claim: Trace volume grows with device count, so a fleet localizes the lost factor from the cheapest records first (scheduler records, then job timelines, then step traces) and captures short targeted traces or statistical samples only where the suspected factor lives.

concepts.label: Scheduling goodput
concepts.claim: Capacity counts only while held by a complete allocation, so partial gangs, fragmentation, and unmet demand are scheduling losses whose levers belong to orchestration.

concepts.label: Runtime goodput
concepts.claim: Allocated time counts only while it produces steps a checkpoint retains at the job's fault-free rate, so startup, input stalls, checkpoint pauses, restarts, and rework add up to the runtime loss.

concepts.label: Program goodput
concepts.claim: Program goodput measures retained step time against a named hardware ideal, reported as MFU against peak arithmetic (counting only the operations the model requires) or as MBU against the bandwidth floor for bandwidth-bound decode.

concepts.label: Trading between goodput factors
concepts.claim: A lever that raises one factor and lowers another is judged by the product, and the efficiency frontier places operating points by goodput, cost, and time to result.

concepts.label: Composed re-profiled optimization
concepts.claim: A local fix reaches the fleet only through the Fleet Law term it shortens, and speedups do not add, so the order of fixes is set by the measured limit and the step is re-profiled after each one.

concepts.label: Tensor-parallel collectives under contention
concepts.claim: In a tensor-parallel replica the per-layer activation AllReduces are launch- and protocol-bound at small batch, so a faster link barely helps, and communication streams contend with compute for the same SMs and memory.

concepts.label: Graph compilation amortization
concepts.claim: A compiled artifact, including the collectives compiler-derived partitioning (GSPMD) inserts, pays back across every job and replica that reuses it, while per-replica builds and recompiles are a runtime-goodput loss.

concepts.label: Serving cost dominance
concepts.claim: Lifetime cost is training once plus cost per query times traffic times deployment time, so at high volume serving overtakes training within days to weeks and the lever is cost per completed request at a fixed mix, quality, and SLO.

concepts.label: SLO goodput and the serving tax
concepts.claim: Serving capacity is the rate of completed requests that meet stated TTFT and per-token targets for a fixed mix, and end-to-end latency adds network, serialization, coordination, and queueing to model time, so a 70 ms model in a 100 ms budget leaves 30 ms for everything else.

concepts.label: Batch formation trades waiting for reuse
concepts.claim: With batch service time t_0 + B t_req throughput saturates toward 1/t_req past a knee near t_0/t_req, and request latency is queueing plus formation plus execution, so a batching window caps formation but not queueing, while Little's law (in-flight work = arrival rate x mean latency) sizes the concurrency and replica count a target rate and latency imply.

concepts.label: Iteration-level batching
concepts.claim: Fixed batch membership strands slots when output lengths differ, and admitting requests at iteration boundaries recovers that capacity only when requests are waiting, KV memory is free, and per-iteration scheduling is cheap relative to a decode step.

concepts.label: Prefill-decode interference and chunked prefill
concepts.claim: Prefill sits far above the ridge while decode intensity grows roughly linearly with batch, so batching buys a large cost-per-token cut until KV capacity stops it, and a monolithic prefill colocated with active streams lands in every decoder's per-token latency, which chunked prefill caps per iteration by moving rather than removing the cost into the long prompt's time to first token; separate prefill and decode pools remove the interference instead but pay alpha + KV bytes / beta per handoff, so disaggregation earns that transfer cost only through measured goodput.

concepts.label: KV cache as admission budget
concepts.claim: KV bytes per token = 2 x layers x KV heads x head dimension x bytes, so maximum batch is free HBM over context times bytes per token, weight fit does not establish serving capacity, and each lever changes a different factor; resident LoRA adapters draw on the same HBM pool, so adapter locality is an admission decision, and preempting a running request means choosing to retain, swap, recompute, or reject its KV state against the waiting request's deadline.

concepts.label: Serving parallelism chosen by the SLO
concepts.claim: Weight bytes set the minimum shard count, but latency follows the per-request Fleet Law, so tensor parallelism divides layer compute while paying collectives per token whose fixed latency dominates decode and keeps it inside one fast domain.

concepts.label: State-aware request routing
concepts.claim: Two random probes cut the maximum load from log n / log log n to log log n in the static model, but serving needs a work signal (active tokens, remaining decode, KV pressure) and atomic admit-or-reject because probes go stale and requests differ fiftyfold in remaining work; across regions the balancer first filters by data-placement policy, artifact version, readiness, and capacity and only then chooses by measured latency or cost.

concepts.label: Paged KV allocation and prefix sharing
concepts.claim: Contiguous maximum-length reservation strands most reserved KV memory, and paged allocation through per-sequence block tables bounds waste to the last block and lets compatible prefixes share physical blocks copy-on-write.

concepts.label: Serving precision decision
concepts.claim: The roofline regime picks the format, weight-only low-bit formats for bandwidth-bound decode and weight-activation W8A8 or FP8 for compute-bound prefill, with block-wise scaling containing weight outliers and PTQ tried before QAT, so a precision change is deployed only for the resource that binds and only with quality measured beside throughput, and the runtime must keep the packed format resident, select supported kernels, and plan KV around real allocations.

concepts.label: Speculative decoding
concepts.claim: A draft model proposes K tokens that the target verifies in one pass while preserving its distribution, so the gain depends on acceptance rate, draft cost, and spare compute, and it vanishes as batching consumes decode's compute headroom.

concepts.label: Per-request compute budget
concepts.claim: Serial reasoning tokens multiply latency by the ratio of reasoning tokens to answer tokens and extend KV residency, so test-time compute is a recurring serving cost per request whose budget must be stated in both time and capacity and justified by measured quality gain.

concepts.label: Overload containment
concepts.claim: A slowing replica becomes a fleet failure when timeouts and retries consume neighbors' headroom, so circuit breakers withdraw it, backpressure pushes overload upstream to admission control, and deadlines travel with cancellation.

concepts.label: Token-denominated tenant isolation
concepts.claim: Pooling tenants raises utilization only with enforced isolation, so quotas bound request rate, concurrency, input and output tokens, KV pages, and accelerator time, checked and reserved atomically.

concepts.label: Phase-aware autoscaling and cold start
concepts.claim: Average utilization is the wrong control signal, so scaling acts on outstanding work against phase-specific service rates with asymmetric hysteresis, and a large-model cold start takes minutes that a ready reserve must cover.

concepts.label: Tail latency under fan-out
concepts.claim: A request that waits for N independent leaves is slow with probability 1 - (1 - q)^N, so 100 leaves at their own p99 leave about 63 percent of requests slow and holding the request at p99 needs each leaf near p99.99, which makes fan-out width a tail cost that fewer shards, queue-aware routing, deadlines with partial results, and hedging each attack.

concepts.label: Local training must earn its place
concepts.claim: Centralized, local-only, and federated learning differ in what crosses the device boundary, and local training is justified only when a measured adaptation gain beats feature-based personalization under privacy and resource constraints.

concepts.label: Update working set within the background allowance
concepts.claim: An on-device update must fit its peak training working set inside the allowance the OS grants a background task, a few hundred MB on a phone rather than its installed RAM, so a model whose weights fit easily can still fail to train.

concepts.label: Background adaptation admission
concepts.claim: The runtime admits an adaptation window only if its energy, thermal, and foreground-latency tests all hold, charging relaxes only the energy test, and admission is revoked when the measured envelope changes.

concepts.label: FedAvg under sampling and non-IID data
concepts.claim: FedAvg is local SGD under a sampled cohort and non-IID shards, so local epochs that save uplink rounds also pull clients toward their own optima (client drift), and the comparison is measured time to a quality target, not rounds.

concepts.label: Participation selection
concepts.claim: Passing the device admission test correlates with hardware, charging habits, and connectivity, so the federated model learns from the admitted population rather than the deployed one, and over-selection with a round deadline concentrates that bias; the skew is sized per cohort as a coverage ratio, the cohort's share of completed updates over its share of the deployed population.

concepts.label: Federated uplink budget
concepts.claim: Per-round traffic is downlink plus uplink plus protocol plus retry over a slow asymmetric uplink, so a small compressed update is not an end-to-end saving once cumulative uploads overtake the raw-data volume.

concepts.label: Secure aggregation
concepts.claim: Data locality is not privacy, because updates and metadata still leak, so secure aggregation's cancelling pairwise masks hide each client's update from the coordinator at the cost of a participation floor (a secret-sharing threshold of survivors, and enough clients that the sum hides each one) and dropout recovery (survivors' shares rebuild a dropped client's masks in an extra round), while differential privacy bounds a different boundary.

concepts.label: Adaptive fleet release policy
concepts.claim: Once models learn after release the release artifact is an adaptation policy versioned with its base model, adapters, and schemas, rollback must restore a compatible set, a shadow comparison against a frozen model is a gate, not a judge, and fleet promotion adds hardware-in-the-loop validation, compatibility across long version skew, and a hold when a cohort's reporting coverage is too low to count as evidence.

concepts.label: Adaptation method by budget term
concepts.claim: Freezing removes a parameter's gradient and optimizer state but not its place on the backward path, so bias-only updates, LoRA, and residual adapters each shrink a different term of the peak-memory budget.

concepts.label: Scarce local evidence allocation
concepts.claim: On-device data is sparse, weakly labeled, non-IID, and unshuffleable, so few-shot sets, streaming updates, replay buffers, and compressed representations each spend a different scarce resource, and an embedding is not anonymized by being low-dimensional.

concepts.label: On-device drift and forgetting
concepts.claim: Sequential local updates that each pass the budget and a local metric can compound into catastrophic forgetting and drift from the validated release, so stability needs a mechanism priced in device state and forgetting measured per cohort.

concepts.label: Personalization state boundary
concepts.claim: The federated objective guarantees nothing per client, so personalization adds per-client state regularized toward the global model and must declare which state is aggregated and which stays local.

concepts.label: Version-compatible aggregation
concepts.claim: A returned update is meaningful only against its base version and schema, so the coordinator binds updates to version and round, reconciles devices returning after days offline, and down-weights stale contributions in buffered asynchronous aggregation.

concepts.label: Operational load follows coupling
concepts.claim: Once models share features, embeddings, pipelines, alerts, and capacity, the operational object is the dependency graph, so pairwise conflicts grow toward N^2/2 and a new model's marginal cost depends on how it couples to the portfolio.

concepts.label: Dependency-aware registry
concepts.claim: Per-model validation does not establish compatibility along a chain, so the registry records upstream and downstream edges whose traversal yields the impact set, and a release names a compatible version set whose rollback unit may span a pipeline.

concepts.label: Feature consistency contract
concepts.claim: A feature store makes training-serving consistency a testable platform invariant only if freshness SLOs name their timestamp contract and point-in-time joins filter on availability time rather than event time.

concepts.label: Staged rollout exposure budget
concepts.claim: Rollout risk is probability of regression times per-unit impact times exposed units, so a canary stage lasts at least its planned sample over traffic share, and the slowest outcome the release must observe sets the schedule.

concepts.label: Evaluation contract
concepts.claim: A fleet release is accepted against one versioned record that pins, for the same artifact, offline, system, responsibility, online, and recovery evidence, each with an owner and an invalidation rule fixed before exposure.

concepts.label: Hierarchical fleet alerting
concepts.claim: With M independent checks the chance of at least one false alert 1 - (1 - p)^M approaches certainty, so monitoring routes by a business, portfolio, model, and infrastructure hierarchy with an owner per level, correlates anomalies to find shared causes, joins metrics, logs, and traces under stable identifiers across jobs, models, and infrastructure, and runs calibrated drift statistics whose responsibility ends when evidence reaches the model owner's update decision.

concepts.label: SLO vector of budgets
concepts.claim: An endpoint can return HTTP 200 while serving stale features or degraded predictions, so each service carries an SLO vector (availability, latency, freshness, quality) with burn rates, and any exhausted dimension stops promotion.

concepts.label: Utilization as the economic invariant
concepts.claim: Owned capacity pays a capital step then a shallow operating slope while rental grows with use, so ownership wins only above a sustained useful-utilization threshold whose value depends on the cost boundary drawn, and the same invariant prices every headroom reserve.

concepts.label: Fleet experiment budgeting
concepts.claim: A release experiment's sample grows as one over the squared effect size, uncorrected multiple tests and peeking inflate false rejections, and interference between concurrent experiments must be budgeted like sample size.

concepts.label: Incident containment and attribution
concepts.claim: ML incidents can leave every service-health signal green, so response applies a known safe containment before root cause is certain, attributes by which models degrade together, and converts each incident into a control.

concepts.label: ML platform as a product
concepts.claim: An internal ML platform centralizes recurring operational judgment at a chosen abstraction level and needs its own SLOs, interface compatibility guarantees, and retirement dates, judged by the work it removes from model teams; namespace tenancy and the team's placement (centralized, embedded, or hybrid) decide where its invariants are enforced.

concepts.label: Platform break-even
concepts.claim: Platform benefit-cost ratio is linear in the number of models at fixed savings, so break-even portfolio size moves with savings per model and platform cost, and recovered hours are capacity, not cash, until spending is avoided; savings per model come from measured recurring technical debt, ranked by impact times frequency times benefit over resolution cost.

concepts.label: Lifecycle TCO
concepts.claim: TCO = C_train + C_infer + C_data + C_iter over one accounting horizon with each cost counted once, the dominant term, which shifts with workload regime, picks the optimization, and FinOps makes the accounting act by metering spend per team, service, and model under attribution rules that shape incentives and an owner who can stop a run.

concepts.label: Capacity planning under lead time
concepts.claim: Capacity takes months to years to acquire while traffic changes in days, so the plan sizes the fleet from the token budget and sustained throughput, follows the longest supply or facility prerequisite as its critical path, and treats late capacity as a reliability failure, not a procurement delay.

concepts.label: ML threat model
concepts.claim: Attacks on a learned system arrive through interfaces the fleet exposes on purpose, so a threat model writes down asset, trust boundary, adversary capability and goal, and control, and keeps model visibility separate from write capability; the serving interface adds prompt injection, which crosses the boundary between instructions and data, and denial of wallet, which spends the cost budget while the endpoint stays available.

concepts.label: Extraction budgets
concepts.claim: Exact artifact theft and approximate behavioral theft need different controls, and because a daily rate limit slows collection without capping its lifetime total, query-based extraction is bounded by cumulative per-principal budgets and the output contract.

concepts.label: Poisoning as a bilevel attack
concepts.claim: A poisoner needs write access to something the model learns from and solves a bilevel problem over the defender's training, so targeted, backdoor, and subpopulation attacks can leave aggregate validation accuracy unchanged, and clean-label poisons that keep every label correct pass any label audit, as concept poisoning of a text-to-image model (Nightshade) shows at a dose of a few hundred images.

concepts.label: Breakdown point of the gradient mean
concepts.claim: In synchronous data parallelism one compromised worker contributes to every replica's update and the mean's breakdown point is zero, so integrity needs robust aggregation rules whose gather-based traffic exceeds a ring AllReduce's.

concepts.label: Security controls priced on a C3 axis
concepts.claim: Every isolation and confidentiality control spends capacity in a specific Fleet Law term, so encrypting bandwidth-bound collectives slows T_comm and partitioning, scrubbing, and tenant-scoped caches strand capacity or forfeit hits.

concepts.label: Provenance bounds trust
concepts.claim: A model can be trusted only as far as a verifiable record of its data, code, weights, and hardware extends, so signatures establish origin but not benign content, and the release record must bind every input the artifact depends on.

concepts.label: Leakage through authorized outputs
concepts.claim: Persistent learning means a correctly executing model can leak its training data through authorized queries (membership in one bit, properties by inversion, verbatim records by memorization), so storage access control cannot protect it, an empirical membership-inference audit is only a lower bound on that leakage, and differential privacy supplies the upper bound.

concepts.label: Differential privacy
concepts.claim: (epsilon, delta)-differential privacy bounds how much one protected unit can change a release, named by an adjacency relation, so it holds against any auxiliary information, and noise scaled to sensitivity over epsilon costs small groups the most.

concepts.label: Hardware trust questions
concepts.claim: Hardware security is four narrow deployment decisions (processor isolation, physical access and fault injection, side-channel observability, provenance and lifecycle trust), each answered by one primitive, and fleet procurement correlates their failure.

concepts.label: Privacy techniques by excluded observer
concepts.claim: De-identification and k-anonymity constrain only the shape of a released table, and federated learning, secure aggregation, homomorphic encryption, secure computation, and synthetic data each exclude a different observer, and none of them bounds what the released model or aggregate reveals.

concepts.label: Privacy budget account
concepts.claim: Privacy loss accumulates across every data-dependent release about the same population, so DP-SGD's many sampled steps need a tested accountant whose recorded inputs (sampling, noise, steps, clipping, adjacency) form the release record, and the cumulative budget becomes a release gate.

concepts.label: Robustness per failure class
concepts.claim: Drift, adversarial inputs, poisoning, and silent faults can keep every service-health signal green while predictions become invalid, and replication does not remove a weakness every copy shares, so robustness is claimed only per stated failure class.

concepts.label: Shift taxonomy
concepts.claim: Covariate shift changes P(x), label shift changes P(y), and concept drift changes P(y|x), so input monitors can be silent under pure concept drift and the type of shift selects the remedy (reweighting, recalibration, or adaptation on fresh labels).

concepts.label: Drift alert to model update
concepts.claim: A drift alert opens an investigation rather than a retrain: detection, correlation with outcome performance, and action are separate levels, and a model update needs labels that confirm the shift and a root cause the update addresses.

concepts.label: Per-request competence contract
concepts.claim: Population monitors cannot say whether one request lies inside demonstrated competence, so serving trades coverage against selective risk along a threshold, and conformal prediction adds a coverage guarantee that holds only under exchangeability.

concepts.label: Adversarial robustness for a named threat model
concepts.claim: Attacker access defines the evaluation a defense must survive (for a physical attack, the full sensor loop rather than saved images), and robustness is bought empirically in training compute (adversarial training multiplies passes per batch) or certifiably in serving samples.

concepts.label: Layered poisoning defense
concepts.claim: Because poisoned records can preserve clean aggregate accuracy, defense runs as ordered layers along the data path (ingress controls, anomaly detection and sanitization, robust training, post-training checks), each with a named blind spot, made reversible by lineage.

concepts.label: Generative reliability
concepts.claim: A hallucination rate is meaningful only against a stated evidence source, prompt set, and decoding settings, and entropy and self-consistency are priced routing signals, not factuality scores.

concepts.label: Distinguishing faults from shift
concepts.claim: A preprocessing bug moves feature statistics like covariate shift and a numerical overflow flips decisions like an adversarial example, so operators read system evidence (timing against releases, fixed-input replay, cross-layer correlation) before choosing a defense.

concepts.label: Adversarial transferability
concepts.claim: Adversarial examples crafted on a surrogate often transfer to the deployed model, which makes black-box attacks practical without gradient access.

concepts.label: Power ceiling versus energy account
concepts.claim: A facility cannot draw more than its grid feed and cooling capacity at any instant, while run energy integrates average power over time, so a short run can be infeasible at modest energy and a long run feasible at large energy.

concepts.label: Sustainability measurement contract
concepts.claim: An energy or carbon number supports a comparison only when it extends the reproducible measurement contract with five fields, the functional unit, system boundary, attribution rule, carbon signal, and time and location of operation.

concepts.label: Operational carbon chain
concepts.claim: Operational CO2 = IT energy x PUE x grid carbon intensity, three terms acting at separate tiers, and PUE measures only non-IT overhead, so a coal-fed site can beat a hydro-fed one on PUE.

concepts.label: Embodied carbon allocation
concepts.claim: Manufacturing emissions are fixed before first power-on and allocated to work by a declared rule, so their share of a job's footprint rises on clean grids and at low utilization and decides when replacing hardware pays.

concepts.label: Dominant lifecycle carbon term
concepts.claim: Lifecycle CO2 is training plus inference plus embodied, where development multiplies training and inference recurs with query volume and idle capacity, so for widely served models inference is usually the dominant term and picks the lever.

concepts.label: Carbon-aware placement and time-shifting
concepts.claim: Moving work to cleaner regions or hours changes the emissions factor, not the energy, so it must use a marginal signal from a forecast, meet deadline, data, capacity, and reliability constraints, and beat the cost of the move.

concepts.label: Water accounting
concepts.claim: Evaporative heat rejection lowers facility energy at the price of water, so water is a separate, location-weighted account (WUE at the IT boundary, withdrawal vs consumption, direct vs indirect) traded against energy.

concepts.label: Demand outruns efficiency
concepts.claim: Fleet energy is energy per job times number of jobs, and demand outruns efficiency twice, through scaling laws that price each loss reduction in multiplicative compute and through rebound, so efficiency targets need absolute budgets.

concepts.label: Facility overhead boundary
concepts.claim: PUE is facility energy over IT energy, defined once at the facility boundary, so budgeting by accelerator TDP underestimates load and the boundary decides where each loss is counted: upstream transformer, UPS, and distribution losses raise PUE while supply and regulator losses stay in IT load.

concepts.label: Energy crossover versus performance ridge
concepts.claim: Modeled energy crosses over from movement-dominated to arithmetic-dominated at an intensity set by energy per byte over energy per operation, a different point from the performance ridge, so batch-1 decode spends most of its energy moving bytes.

concepts.label: Edge and federated energy accounting
concepts.claim: Local execution saves energy only when the radio, remote compute, and transfers it avoids exceed the device's added compute, idle power, and manufacturing, so edge and federated deployment move energy rather than remove it.

concepts.label: Assurance case
concepts.claim: A registry proves which weights shipped, not that shipping was justified, so deployment is justified by a versioned assurance case (claim for a stated use, argument, evidence, assumptions, an owner who can block, an invalidation rule) that expires on material change and maps the applicable legal obligations onto the lifecycle.

concepts.label: Fairness criteria conflict
concepts.claim: Demographic parity, equalized odds, equality of opportunity, and calibration measure different conditional rates, one classifier can fail all of them at once, and they cannot all hold when base rates differ, so choosing one is a governance decision.

concepts.label: Disparity measurement uncertainty
concepts.claim: A subgroup gap is evidence only with denominators, confidence intervals, and coverage limits, single-axis audits hide intersectional failure, and a significant disparity says nothing about its cause.

concepts.label: Fleet fairness monitoring
concepts.claim: Continuous fairness telemetry costs streaming counters per group and metric, runs mostly off the request path, updates prediction-only metrics at once while label-dependent metrics wait for outcomes, and reports under-supported groups as insufficient, not zero.

concepts.label: Safeguards as capacity
concepts.claim: Every responsible-AI control consumes budgeted training, serving, memory, storage, or human-review capacity on a specific path, and where it is placed decides who is protected.

concepts.label: Machine unlearning
concepts.claim: A privacy guarantee bounds exposure but does not remove a record from trained weights, so deletion that reaches model state needs a removal method and evidence, and its cost (full retraining vs sharded retraining) is set by architecture chosen before training.

concepts.label: Contestability and remedy
concepts.claim: Explanation serves accountability only when an affected person can challenge a decision and obtain correction, which requires decision provenance, audience-appropriate reasons, an appeal routed to an authorized reviewer, and tracked outcomes.

concepts.label: Sociotechnical feedback and designed oversight
concepts.claim: Deployed models reshape their own future data and their operators, so predictions can become self-fulfilling in ways a static test set cannot detect, and human oversight must be designed against both automation bias and alert fatigue.

concepts.label: Threshold postprocessing and the fairness cost
concepts.claim: Group-specific thresholds can equalize a chosen rate but leave score calibration unchanged, need authorized sensitive attributes at decision time, and carry a scenario-specific accuracy cost.

concepts.label: Explanation placement
concepts.claim: Explanation method and placement are fixed by audience, deadline, and attribution cost (saliency, exact tree attribution, sampled Shapley values), and attribution is not causation.

concepts.label: Generative governance surfaces
concepts.claim: For a generative fleet, fairness, privacy, and safety are governed through system prompts, retrieved context, reward models, policy classifiers, and output filters, all versioned as infrastructure.

concepts.label: Bounded autonomy and safety case
concepts.claim: When a system acts faster than anyone can review its decisions, the objective itself becomes a governed artifact and trust is operationalized as a safety case over a validated envelope with runtime guardrails, because fleet scale turns rare failures into expected incidents.

concepts.label: Privacy claims name their boundary
concepts.claim: A privacy guarantee covers only the data path its mechanism accounts for, so differentially private training says nothing about private inputs copied into service logs, and each claim must state which accesses it covers.

volumes.label: III
volumes.title: Agentic ML Systems
volumes.description: Context, tools, authority, and durable execution.

concepts.label: Agency is a property of the closed loop
concepts.claim: A system is agentic when a runtime, not a human, closes the proposal-action-observation loop, so the model's output is a proposal with no standing authority and enforcement, isolation, persistence, and completion checks belong to the runtime.

concepts.label: Trajectory as the unit of engineering
concepts.claim: The ordered record of states, proposals, runtime decisions, and observations from initial context to acceptance, termination, or escalation is the accounting boundary for cost, latency, state lifetime, quotas, and permissions, so resources are managed per task rather than per call.

concepts.label: H·S·A exposures
concepts.claim: A task's coordinate is its horizon H in turns, carried state S0 to S3, and authority A0 to A3, each level set by operational consequence rather than command syntax, and the coordinate names the exposure that closure must answer.

concepts.label: Invariant closure
concepts.claim: Constraints never rest on the model: bounds close mechanically below it and acceptance rests on external evidence above it, and greater exposure demands stronger closure.

concepts.label: Task contract
concepts.claim: A goal with negative scope, an environment, permitted actions, available observations, and completion criteria turn intent into something the runtime can enforce, and each omitted field produces a specific, predictable failure.

concepts.label: Horizon compounding
concepts.claim: With independent unchecked steps Pr(success) = (1-eps)^H, so the product eps*H rather than step accuracy sets reliability, and a check plus restoration that shortens the unchecked segment is the cheaper lever.

concepts.label: Cost per accepted task
concepts.claim: Under retry-until-accept, C_eff = E[C_attempt]/p_acc, so acceptance divides the whole attempt cost and any mechanism pays for its overhead only if it lowers this ratio.

concepts.label: Six-phase turn lifecycle
concepts.claim: Every turn passes context assembly, model invocation, validate-and-authorize, tool execution, observation, and assessment against the contract, and only the second phase belongs to the model.

concepts.label: Fail-plausible fault
concepts.claim: The characteristic agent failure is well-formed, credible, and wrong, so fail-stop monitors record success and agreement among samples from one model sets no bound on wrong answers.

concepts.label: Zero ambient authority
concepts.claim: Every side effect passes an explicit runtime-checked grant and evidence comes only from tools and deterministic checks, never from model text.

concepts.label: Closure evidence levels
concepts.claim: Self-report, static analysis, visible tests, sealed tests, and formal verification form a default ordering of acceptance evidence that coverage can override, and every check is a bounded claim narrower than the task.

concepts.label: Fixed workflow vs model-directed loop
concepts.claim: A model-directed loop is justified only where open-ended evidence must be interpreted and it raises acceptance by more than it inflates attempt cost under the same contract and verifier.

concepts.label: Side-effect classes
concepts.claim: Authority levels A0 to A3 (read-only, disposable workspace, compensable, irreversible) classify an action by its consequence in the environment, and the same command can change class when the environment changes.

concepts.label: Lighthouse workloads
concepts.claim: The repair, research, remediation, and support agents each bind on a different constraint (compounding and resend, untrusted input and fan-out, blast radius and approval latency, tail latency and session state) and recur as the volume's running cases.

concepts.label: Tool-wait problem
concepts.claim: A trajectory that waits on a tool must decouple task lifetime from the serving allocation, or retained state occupies scarce memory while no tokens are produced.

concepts.label: Outcome taxonomy
concepts.claim: Every trajectory ends accepted, failed, unresolved, or escalated, budget exhaustion is unresolved rather than failure, and silent termination is a defect.

concepts.label: Proposal boundary
concepts.claim: Model output is a proposal with zero ambient authority: the runtime validates, authorizes, executes, and returns the observation, so a tool request is never an effect and a model claim is never an observation.

concepts.label: Token-measured admission
concepts.claim: A request is admitted only if its fully serialized wire payload, counted with the target model's own tokenizer, satisfies S <= S_max - K_max, and hidden reasoning tokens debit the same output headroom.

concepts.label: Sampling shapes candidates, not correctness
concepts.claim: Temperature, top-k, and top-p reshape which candidates appear but none makes a likely token a correct one, so sampling settings are chosen by measured task pass rates.

concepts.label: Recorded calls replay, served calls do not
concepts.claim: Reduction order and serving-path changes flip contested argmax choices even at temperature zero, so the runtime logs model revision, serving configuration, and sampling settings with every call and replays recorded responses when behavior must be reproduced.

concepts.label: Invocation contract
concepts.claim: Every call is a request record plus a normalized status envelope, and only a COMPLETED reply enters the candidate path, so a truncated prefix that parses is quarantined and a local deadline expiry leaves the remote outcome unknown.

concepts.label: Checks certify named properties
concepts.claim: Likelihood is not truth, schema conformance is not permission, a passing test covers only exercised behavior, and self-review re-samples the same distribution, so each gate is chosen for the one property it certifies and a fallible checker leaves a residual defect share given by Bayes.

concepts.label: Output-bound call latency
concepts.claim: Prefill is bounded by arithmetic and unbatched decode by weight bandwidth, so one output token costs roughly as much time as several hundred prompt tokens and output length is the primary latency lever.

concepts.label: Quadratic resend and prefix reuse
concepts.claim: Re-sending an append-only history submits H*S0 + Delta*H(H-1)/2 prompt tokens, compatible prefix reuse cuts fresh prefill to S0 + (H-1)*Delta, and latency, work, and billed dollars remain separate accounts.

concepts.label: Grammar-constrained decoding
concepts.claim: A per-state logit mask guarantees a completed output is in the enforced language, but only for syntax, only on COMPLETED status, and an over-constrained schema forces confabulation unless it offers an explicit unknown variant.

concepts.label: Interface choice under matched budgets
concepts.claim: Representation granularity, serialization, and constraint mechanism are independent interface axes judged on accepted outcomes under matched budgets, with a deadline acting as an admission filter and every initiated trial kept in the denominator.

concepts.label: Allocation axes
concepts.claim: Depth, breadth, and feedback can spend the same output ceiling yet differ in critical path, retained KV state, and bill, and only feedback adds information the prompt and weights lack.

concepts.label: Budgeted deliberation
concepts.claim: Test-time compute is a per-decision allowance that sets the attempt cost in C_eff, so it pays only when it raises acceptance faster than cost, and difficulty should route the budget.

concepts.label: Coverage is not selection
concepts.claim: pass@k = 1-(1-p)^k caps any selector that returns an unchanged pool member, while realized accuracy is set by the selector, so coverage near 98 percent can coexist with a vote that plateaus near half.

concepts.label: Ranking is not acceptance
concepts.claim: Voting and learned ranking both return the best failure from a defective pool, so only selection by a check the candidate cannot modify justifies returning a candidate instead of abstaining.

concepts.label: Verifier precision
concepts.claim: The precision of a passing verdict depends on the valid-candidate base rate and the check's error rates, not on pool size, so a larger pool raises both the chance of a selection and the chance of a false pass.

concepts.label: Selection pressure
concepts.claim: Argmax over N noisy scores selects positive error growing like sigma*sqrt(2 ln N) and crowns any exploit present in the pool, so check accuracy must be re-measured on selected candidates.

concepts.label: Step-level evidence
concepts.claim: Outcome checks execute a finished candidate while reward models only predict quality, and step checks prune failing branches early at the cost of false rejections and scorer input that grows quadratically without prefix reuse.

concepts.label: Revisable candidate plans
concepts.claim: Recording a candidate as a dependency graph of artifacts with evidence provenance lets a refuting observation invalidate exactly its descendants while retained branches keep their support.

concepts.label: Search tree pruning
concepts.claim: A step check that rejects a fraction r of b children gives an effective branching factor b(1-r), so a tree stays finite on its own only when r > 1-1/b and otherwise needs hard caps.

concepts.label: Search accounting
concepts.claim: A search tracks money, non-interchangeable work, wall time, and peak live state in separate accounts and reserves each request's maximum charge before dispatch, releasing it only on settlement.

concepts.label: Stopping precedence
concepts.claim: Before admitting more work, apply hard ceilings, then satisficing, then marginal stopping, and an exhausted budget returns unresolved or escalates rather than lowering the acceptance threshold.

concepts.label: Deliberation operating point
concepts.claim: A deliberation policy's operating point is chosen on the cost-acceptance-deadline frontier, with false acceptance, abstention, and deadline exhaustion reported separately.

concepts.label: Working-set partition
concepts.claim: Before each call the runtime selects a bounded working set and splits the input allowance S_max - K_max among instructions, tool declarations, task state, and observations, and appended observations are the term that grows and displaces task state.

concepts.label: Usable working context
concepts.claim: Usable context is an empirical property of a model, configuration, representation, and workload found by decision-level evaluation, because attention dilutes a target key as staged keys accumulate and position matters.

concepts.label: Change-rate ordering
concepts.claim: Staging the request as root, trunk, and leaf by change rate keeps the longest exact token prefix reusable, so volatile fields belong in the leaf, although correctness always overrides cache economics.

concepts.label: Scope rule
concepts.claim: An observation is evidence only for the artifact versions and execution conditions under which it was gathered, and provenance labels on untrusted spans guide interpretation but enforce nothing.

concepts.label: Context compaction
concepts.claim: Every compaction is a lossy transform that can silently drop evidence a later decision needs, so the runtime pins a protected-field set and keeps handles to raw records.

concepts.label: Audited progress records
concepts.claim: A model-written continuation record is an untrusted candidate that a host-side audit checks against a runtime-owned field inventory, the event log, and the workspace version before it replaces history.

concepts.label: Context invalidation
concepts.claim: A verified write withdraws current-state authority from bound observations and flags dependent conclusions for reassessment, without erasing their historical truth.

concepts.label: Context policy evaluation
concepts.claim: Context policies are compared as complete policies on accepted outcomes under a fixed model, tools, budget, and fixture, and retention or compression ratios are diagnostics with explicit denominators, not verdicts.

concepts.label: Hysteretic compaction scheduling
concepts.claim: Separating a trigger watermark from a post-compaction target sets compaction cadence, and the amortized pass cost is judged against cost per accepted task, not local turn cost.

concepts.label: KV footprint and resident fit
concepts.claim: Retained attention state costs 2 x layers x KV heads x head dim x bytes per token, so resident fit in the KV pool falls as 1/S with context length, and the attention design fixed at pretraining sets the slope.

concepts.label: Paged KV allocation
concepts.claim: Fixed-size blocks mapped by a per-sequence block table remove the stranded memory of full-cap reservation and bound tail waste below one block.

concepts.label: Copy-on-write block sharing
concepts.claim: Forked candidates share prefix blocks by reference count, so a fork costs block-table entries rather than a payload copy and physical demand is the count of unique blocks.

concepts.label: Radix prefix cache
concepts.claim: A content-keyed radix tree finds the longest retained common prefix, leaf-first eviction keeps residency prefix-closed, and efficacy is the token-weighted hit rate after availability, permission, and block rounding.

concepts.label: Reusable is not applicable
concepts.claim: A reusable prefix must be compatible, available, and permitted, and none of the three says whether the evidence is current, so freshness is enforced by the harness rewriting the prompt.

concepts.label: Paused-state policy
concepts.claim: During a tool wait the engine keeps, moves, or drops only uniquely reclaimable blocks, and offloading pays only when the wait exceeds the transfer round trip and memory is contested.

concepts.label: Residency tax
concepts.claim: By Little's law a fixed pool of slots sustains a turn rate inversely proportional to residence, so holding state through a synchronous tool wait divides the memory-bound turn rate by 1 + T_tool/T_model.

concepts.label: Lossy KV approximation
concepts.claim: Token eviction, sliding windows, and KV quantization change the computation and must be validated against an agent's hard semantic dependencies, such as dormant constraints and exact identifiers, rather than perplexity.

concepts.label: Chunked prefill
concepts.claim: Splitting an uncached prompt into chunks under a per-iteration token budget bounds the inter-token gap of ongoing streams to one iteration at a modest delay to the new request's first token.

concepts.label: Little's law
concepts.claim: Mean occupancy equals arrival rate times mean residence (L = lambda W), a mean identity that sizes slot pools but says nothing about peaks.

concepts.label: Record roles
concepts.claim: Persistent records are roles in an evidence chain (source of record, observation log, agent-written memory, retrieval index), not storage tiers, and any claim is validated against its source of record.

concepts.label: Retrieval contract
concepts.claim: Every read is a bounded request answered by an envelope that reports scope, snapshot, completeness status, and per-item provenance, and an empty result proves nonexistence only for a complete search of the declared scope.

concepts.label: Query formulation choice
concepts.claim: A named target gets a direct read, a predictable unnamed set gets pre-staged, and a chain where each item is found only from the last forces model-directed probing at one model round per dependent hop.

concepts.label: Bounded multi-hop retrieval
concepts.claim: Neighborhoods grow geometrically with traversal depth, so multi-hop retrieval bounds edge types, direction, depth, and visited nodes before ranking.

concepts.label: Memory write policy
concepts.claim: The runtime, not the model, decides what persists: admission checks run before deduplication, same-scope updates supersede by compare-and-swap, and deletion (on request, on withdrawn consent, or at the end of a recorded retention period) is a lifecycle event the store must honor.

concepts.label: Memory poisoning
concepts.claim: Repeated retrieval or re-summarization adds no independent evidence, so preventing a withdrawn or unverified claim from persisting needs a provenance graph over derived records whose invalidation cascades.

concepts.label: Source-generation invalidation
concepts.claim: A retrieval index is a materialized view that cannot be maintained by deltas, so each derived entry carries a source generation and the gateway admits it only for the generations it is valid in.

concepts.label: Memory policy evaluation
concepts.claim: The unit of evaluation is the whole memory policy run through isolated multi-session trials with lifecycle fixtures, scored by task acceptance and cost per accepted task including background maintenance.

concepts.label: Matching method
concepts.claim: Exact lookup, lexical ranking, structural indexes, and dense similarity answer different information needs and fail in different places, and hybrid retrieval joins candidates on full identity.

concepts.label: Exact-scan floor and approximate indexes
concepts.claim: An exact vector scan is bandwidth-bound with floor N*d*b/BW, which screens it against the search budget, while approximate indexes trade recall for bytes touched.

concepts.label: Read-your-writes consistency
concepts.claim: A session must observe its own committed memory writes on later reads, which a lagging index or replica silently violates unless reads are pinned to a generation at or after the write.

concepts.label: Complete mediation
concepts.claim: Every proposed call, reads included, passes a deterministic host reference monitor that validates, authorizes, dispatches with outcome tracking, and shapes the observation.

concepts.label: Action-time preconditions
concepts.claim: A schema settles only structure, so any precondition that depends on current state (an expected version, a canonical path) must be enforced atomically with the effect at the endpoint.

concepts.label: Discovery is not authority
concepts.claim: A shared tool protocol cuts integration to N_host + N_tool adapters, but listed tools supply only interface syntax: descriptions are untrusted input and admitted schemas must be bound to the server instance.

concepts.label: Settlement before retry
concepts.claim: A timeout records that the caller stopped waiting, not that the effect failed, so a dispatched mutation without a reply is an uncertain outcome that blocks retry until its repeat semantics or evidence settle it.

concepts.label: Operation identity
concepts.claim: A logical operation ID names one intended effect across attempts, each attempt gets a fresh attempt ID, and the ID is safe only under an endpoint contract that binds it to caller, scope, and arguments.

concepts.label: Bounded observation
concepts.claim: Capture and staging are separate budgets, so the adapter drains both pipes, enforces byte limits, and stages a head-and-tail view with a typed notice of what was omitted and a handle to the rest.

concepts.label: Acknowledgment is not completion
concepts.claim: A long-running tool returns a job handle whose acknowledgment means only that work was queued, so status keeps last-observed-running distinct from unavailable and from failure, and detection belongs to the runtime.

concepts.label: Toolkit staging
concepts.claim: Which descriptors the model sees each turn and how much work each tool does are design variables priced in context tokens and in cost per accepted task.

concepts.label: Reconciliation probe
concepts.claim: A mutating tool over an endpoint without deduplication ships actuate, probe, and compensate together, with the probe written before dispatch against a captured baseline.

concepts.label: Repeat-behavior classes
concepts.claim: Read, set-desired-state, and produce-another-event classify what a repeated call does, a dimension orthogonal to the authority levels.

concepts.label: Confused deputy
concepts.claim: A program that acts with its own legitimate authority on behalf of a less privileged requester can be steered to misuse that authority, so authority must follow the request, not the program.

concepts.label: Computer-use tool calls
concepts.claim: A click keeps every tool-boundary invariant while losing atomicity, so each observation carries capture, window, and coordinate mapping and target identity is rechecked before dispatch.

concepts.label: Containment beneath the model
concepts.claim: Admitting a well-typed call does not bound what the code it starts can reach, so the limit must be enforced below the executing process by a mechanism the code cannot modify.

concepts.label: In-process restriction fails
concepts.claim: Pruning an interpreter's globals is an interface filter, not an execution boundary, because reachable object references, shared native libraries, and inherited authority leave the supervisor's full power within reach.

concepts.label: Capability grants
concepts.claim: A capability is an unforgeable reference that designates a resource and authorizes operations on it, and a grant admits an access only if the reference is authentic and the operation, object, condition, and expiry all match.

concepts.label: Attenuation and revocation
concepts.claim: A derived grant may only narrow its parent, and chained-caveat tokens let any holder narrow offline but never widen, while attenuation never withdraws the parent grant it came from.

concepts.label: Isolation envelopes
concepts.claim: Shared-kernel containers, user-space kernels, microVMs, and restricted bytecode differ first in where a system call lands, which sets the trusted components and the per-call tax each envelope pays.

concepts.label: Copy-on-write workspace
concepts.claim: A task workspace separates immutable baseline, private modifications, scratch, and exportable artifacts, and copy-on-write makes provisioning cost track what the agent writes rather than what it can see.

concepts.label: Egress control
concepts.claim: Outbound reach is enforced on the host data path with a packet filter and an operation-aware mediator that cover each other's blind spots, never by guest proxy settings.

concepts.label: Reset contract
concepts.claim: A used environment may serve a new tenant only after a reset that fences authority, quiesces owned work, exports permitted outputs, and clears four state domains in order.

concepts.label: Credential brokering
concepts.claim: A host-side broker holds the credential outside the guest and performs only the authorized operation on its behalf, which removes the most valuable target from an injected environment.

concepts.label: Sandbox pool sizing
concepts.claim: Mean active leases follow N_active = lambda * T_hold over the whole trajectory, so pool cost is driven by memory residency over the horizon, and the standby reserve is set by the replenishment window.

concepts.label: Least privilege
concepts.claim: Each component receives only the authority its current task needs, which capabilities make enforceable rather than aspirational.

concepts.label: Ambient authority
concepts.claim: Authority that comes from where a program runs rather than from the request it serves is what an injected or buggy process inherits, and capabilities replace it with explicit grants.

concepts.label: Blast radius
concepts.claim: The set of state and principals an action can damage if it goes wrong bounds the worst-case cost of containment failure and sets how strong a boundary must be.

concepts.label: Structural prompt injection
concepts.claim: Instructions, tool definitions, the request, and every observation are serialized into one token sequence in which no position carries enforced privilege, so injection is structural and exposure grows with every untrusted read.

concepts.label: Callable is not permitted
concepts.claim: Injection turns the runtime into a confused deputy with a legitimate identity, so authorization must judge this request within this task, not the function name, argument types, or endpoint allowlist.

concepts.label: Information-flow labels
concepts.claim: Confidentiality and integrity provenance vary independently, so the host attaches both to every record, propagates them by the lattice join, and checks release and evidence before dispatch.

concepts.label: Quarantined readers
concepts.claim: A quarantined reader keeps raw untrusted text out of the planner and typed handles keep untrusted bytes out of context, but a schema-valid field is still an untrusted claim, not evidence.

concepts.label: Effective permission intersection
concepts.claim: When an agent acts for a requester, effective permission is the intersection of requester rights, service principal, task grant, and issuer and receiver policy, with identities taken from the runtime's task record, never from prompt text.

concepts.label: Action-bound approval
concepts.claim: Human approval binds to a digest of the canonical, host-resolved action, is presented out of band with the agent's explanation labeled untrusted, and is re-verified with its preconditions immediately before dispatch.

concepts.label: Multi-turn policy continuity
concepts.claim: Over a trajectory an attacker gains an adaptation oracle and conversational momentum, so every dispatch is re-evaluated against policy and an obfuscated retry after a block is still the blocked action.

concepts.label: Security outcome measurement
concepts.claim: A defense is evaluated by system effects at the protected sink on whole eligible episodes, not by model text, and its overhead is priced in cost per accepted task.

concepts.label: Lethal trifecta
concepts.claim: An agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and an external communication channel can be steered to exfiltrate, and removing any one leg breaks the attack path.

concepts.label: Prefix-cache timing channel
concepts.claim: A prefix cache shared across security domains leaks through time to first token whether another caller processed identical text, so sharing domains must bound cache reuse.

concepts.label: Detection vs separation
concepts.claim: Detection only lowers the rate at which payloads get through, whereas separation by construction bounds what any payload can reach, detected or not.

concepts.label: Harness owns continuation
concepts.claim: A model that honors a pause or allowance with probability p per turn holds it over H turns only p^H of the time, so the decision to take another step belongs to a harness that treats every reply as an untrusted proposal.

concepts.label: Trajectory record
concepts.claim: Supervision needs one authoritative per-trajectory control record, written only by the harness, holding contract, lifecycle state, accounting, grants, current invocations, the operation table, and a live plan.

concepts.label: Guarded transitions
concepts.claim: The trajectory advances only along legal state-machine edges whose guards pass on a current record version, and admission commits atomically under the record lock before any request leaves the host (register before send).

concepts.label: Settlement rule
concepts.claim: Withdrawing a result's eligibility to inform the model never clears the operation's obligation, and no trajectory reaches a terminal state until every obligation is settled or explicitly transferred.

concepts.label: Turn-boundary control
concepts.claim: Operator control takes effect at turn boundaries, so a harness that checks only when a reply ends lets one call postpone a pause by K_max x t_dec, and pause, interrupt, cancel, kill, and budget stop change admission differently.

concepts.label: Approval escrow
concepts.claim: A proposal that requires review is held undispatched, bound by digest and expiry, and a favorable decision is one precondition rather than an order, so dispatch re-runs the full admission check and silence expires rather than denies.

concepts.label: Bounded-liability admission
concepts.claim: A budget is an enforceable ceiling only if each operation is admitted when actual consumption plus outstanding reservations plus its worst-case liability plus a protected finalization reserve fits the allowance in every dimension.

concepts.label: Trajectory budget vector
concepts.claim: A runaway retry loop is locally compliant at every step, so the harness bounds turns, tokens, wall time, and dollars as one vector, reads the largest used fraction, and escalates through steer, restrict, and finalize.

concepts.label: Supervised waiting
concepts.claim: An asynchronous wait frees the worker thread but not the workspace lease, KV residency, reservations, or deadline, and a wait deadline ends the harness's wait, never the remote operation.

concepts.label: Fair model-call scheduling
concepts.claim: Weighted deficit round-robin charged by each call's full input plus maximum output fixes a class's share of charge, not of calls, and fairness, provider quotas, and budgets are independent gates.

concepts.label: Budget ceiling selection
concepts.claim: A budget ceiling is chosen by evaluating the complete control policy on representative tasks and minimizing cost per accepted task, counting failed and budget-halted attempts.

concepts.label: Budget reservation
concepts.claim: An operation's maximum additional charge is withheld at admission and released only when evidence settles the operation, so ambiguous dispatches stay reserved.

concepts.label: Streaming cancellation
concepts.claim: Cancelling a stream removes the dependence of control latency on output length, and partial or canceled output is quarantined and never dispatched.

concepts.label: Failure-domain durability
concepts.claim: An acknowledgment is durable only against the faults its storage tier survives, so each write's durability is declared against a failure domain rather than assumed.

concepts.label: Trajectory log
concepts.claim: Recovery state comes from an append-only, typed trajectory log, and the live trajectory record is a deterministic fold over that log.

concepts.label: Durable intent before dispatch
concepts.claim: An admitted operation's identity, arguments, grant reference, and reservation must be durable under the declared failure domain before the request leaves, so no effect can exist without its intent on record.

concepts.label: Completeness rule
concepts.claim: Where a crash falls in the ordering decides whether an operation is not dispatched, in doubt, or established, and an absent intent proves non-dispatch only in a complete authoritative log prefix.

concepts.label: Checkpoint binding
concepts.claim: A checkpoint binds the record snapshot, workspace snapshot, artifacts, and reducer versions to one committed log position, captured as a consistent cut and published only after the state it references is durable.

concepts.label: Resume protocol
concepts.claim: Resume is an authorized continuation in ordered stages (prove the prefix, acquire ownership with a fencing epoch, restore by fold, reconcile in-doubt operations) rather than a restart.

concepts.label: Record and replay
concepts.claim: A sampled model reply cannot be regenerated, so reproduction substitutes recorded inputs at nondeterministic boundaries, and one recording serves time-travel inspection, harness regression, and counterfactual branching.

concepts.label: Checkpoint stride
concepts.claim: Young's interval prices checkpoints when a crash loses work to re-execute, and once each turn is logged the stride lengthens by the square root of the cost ratio because a crash costs reconstruction, not resampling.

concepts.label: First-divergence localization
concepts.claim: Debugging two executions steps boundary by boundary from a verified checkpoint to the first mismatch under a declared equivalence, because every later difference may be a consequence.

concepts.label: Recovery retention
concepts.claim: Current recovery, historical replay, and diagnostics need different artifacts on independent schedules, so retention is derived from the declared recovery and replay promise, not storage convenience.

concepts.label: Fencing tokens
concepts.claim: A monotonically increasing owner epoch checked at the resource rejects writes from a stalled holder that outlives its lease, because lease expiry alone is not exclusion.

concepts.label: In-doubt action
concepts.claim: An admitted operation whose effect cannot be proven present or absent is in doubt and must be reconciled before any re-dispatch, the recovery-side view of an uncertain outcome.

concepts.label: Compensation
concepts.claim: An external service and the runtime log share no atomic commit, so an established effect is remediated only by a separately committed forward operation that restores declared postconditions, not the past.

concepts.label: Trajectory saga
concepts.claim: A trajectory saga durably registers each effectful step's cleanup template before dispatch, not after the step returns, so a crash never leaves an effect without its compensator.

concepts.label: Cleanup graph
concepts.claim: Recovery order is a DAG of admitted cleanup operations rather than a reverse stack, and an unresolved node blocks only its transitive dependents.

concepts.label: Recovery decision order
concepts.claim: Transport retry, fresh proposal, feedback repair, compensation, and hold or escalate are chosen by evidence class first, then admission, then expected cost.

concepts.label: Repair break-even
concepts.claim: One bounded repair attempt beats immediate unwind-and-rebuild iff its measured success rate exceeds p* = C_repair / C_fallback, evaluated separately in time and dollars.

concepts.label: Commitment regions
concepts.claim: Reversibility is relative to a subsystem and a grant, so a plan is organized into compensable preparation, a single pivot, and owned follow-up duties, with every check that can precede the pivot hoisted ahead of it.

concepts.label: Semantic watchdog
concepts.claim: A looping trajectory is hyperactive, not dead, so a watchdog compares a declared task projection, verifier results, and repeated action-outcome pairs over a bounded window, and its window sets detection latency.

concepts.label: Incident containment
concepts.claim: On suspicion, fail-safe defaults hold the trajectory at every dispatch boundary without the agent's cooperation while preregistered cleanup runs under a separate narrow grant until residual obligations settle.

concepts.label: Dependency containment
concepts.claim: Scoped circuit breakers, a single retry owner, and bulkheads bound three different quantities when many trajectories share one dependency.

concepts.label: Task acceptance contract
concepts.claim: A trial is credited as an accepted task only when evidence on the exact candidate bytes satisfies its declared outcome, process, resource, and residual-duty criteria, and every verdict is pass, fail, pending, or unknown, with no default to pass.

concepts.label: Hermetic evaluation gym
concepts.claim: Comparable trials need a hermetic boundary that declares which dependencies are provisioned, simulated, or blocked, a versioned task fixture, and a reset that leaves no state for the next trial.

concepts.label: Grader isolation
concepts.claim: Sealed tests protect evidence only if a trusted controller outside both the live agent's reach and the submitted artifact's execution keeps the reference solutions, hidden tests, and score store and binds each verdict to the artifact hash.

concepts.label: Grader calibration
concepts.claim: A grader is characterized only against an independent reference assessment, and its false-acceptance rate and the failure share among accepted results answer different questions.

concepts.label: Task sampling and score intervals
concepts.claim: Repeats shrink only the run-variance term while new tasks shrink both, so evaluation samples tasks rather than runs and reports score intervals instead of point estimates.

concepts.label: Paired comparison
concepts.claim: Configurations are compared on the same sampled tasks with outcome pairs kept together, which cuts the variance of the difference, and noninferiority margins are planned before data.

concepts.label: Matched-budget evaluation
concepts.claim: Policies are compared on a fixed task distribution, criteria, and resource envelope, and budgeted acceptance and observed cost per accepted task charge every initiated trial.

concepts.label: Contamination
concepts.claim: Benchmark tasks or solutions that appeared in pretraining corpora or retrieval indices before the trial invalidate the claim the benchmark supports, and no similarity threshold proves independence.

concepts.label: Repeated-run consistency
concepts.claim: pass@k measures candidate availability while pass^k = E[p_i^k] measures whether all k runs pass, and the two diverge as k grows.

concepts.label: Coverage rule
concepts.claim: A check certifies only the behavior its assertions exercise, so acceptance criteria name what each check covers and what it leaves unverified.

concepts.label: Trajectory traces
concepts.claim: Spans bind every model call, mediated tool execution, and check to their trial and artifact, but a diagnostic trace may sample or drop and never replaces the durable recovery log or the verdict record.

concepts.label: Trace retention
concepts.claim: Sampling may thin diagnostic detail but never the accounting record of admitted trials, verdicts, spend, and drops, and retention is chosen per verdict under storage and privacy budgets.

concepts.label: Postmortem by intervention
concepts.claim: An agent incident is diagnosed by keeping findings separated by boundary and testing each with a controlled intervention on the recorded trajectory, not by naming one culprit.

concepts.label: Staged release
concepts.claim: Release exposure is staged so each stage answers its own question (offline gate, shadow execution, bounded canary), with sequential monitoring and hard tripwires that stop admission.

concepts.label: Release gate
concepts.claim: A release decision is a declared conjunctive rule written before data and applied to an evidence record that keeps verdicts, paired cohorts, and diagnostics.

concepts.label: Critical path
concepts.claim: The longest chain of dependent operations recorded in the trace is measured from span timing, and only work on it can shorten the trajectory.

concepts.label: Empirical safety case
concepts.claim: Release is justified by a scoped, inspectable safety case of claim, argument, evidence, assumptions, and residual uncertainty, and evidence for one claim does not establish the others.

concepts.label: Capability-gap triage
concepts.claim: A failure earns a weight update only if it persists with complete context, a well-formed interface, and a healthy runtime, so counterfactual probes run up the intervention ladder from context and schema to SFT and then RL.

concepts.label: Learning artifacts from one record
concepts.claim: One recorded run can yield imitation material, a preference comparison, or a rollout fixture, and each use has its own admission conditions rather than inheriting the run's outcome.

concepts.label: Task-group splits
concepts.claim: With k attempts per task a random trace split puts most tasks on both sides, so partitions are assigned to task groups that hold every attempt, paraphrase, fork, and derived record.

concepts.label: Admission cascade
concepts.claim: Admission is a route-specific conjunction of predicate families that each resolve to pass, fail, pending, or unknown, a missing check never defaults to pass, and checks are ordered by cost per rejection.

concepts.label: Recovery demonstrations
concepts.claim: A policy trained only on clean prefixes meets off-path states it never saw, so recovery demonstrations keep the mistake as conditioning context and select only the assessed correction as the target.

concepts.label: Self-selection narrowing
concepts.claim: A generate-select-train loop carries contrast only on informative tasks, so it narrows toward what it already solves, and hard and trivial fixtures cost attempts without teaching.

concepts.label: Bounded collection flow
concepts.claim: Collection is an asynchronous pipeline whose staging must be sized for a verifier service-time collapse, not average utilization, with each run holding a collection credit at the record ceiling until durable disposition and cost counted per emitted artifact.

concepts.label: Record lineage
concepts.claim: Every record version carries a lineage envelope, and any transformation creates a derived record that inherits its source's split group and use permission, so withdrawal reaches every descendant.

concepts.label: Mixture specification
concepts.claim: A trajectory class has different shares by records, processed tokens, and selected target tokens, so a mixture is specified in targets and budgeted in processed tokens.

concepts.label: Test-tampering defense
concepts.claim: Grader isolation applied to admission keeps test harnesses, inputs, and verdicts beyond the candidate's reach, because an undetected bypass is reinforced across training iterations.

concepts.label: Three homes for behavior
concepts.claim: Fine-tuning changes only the proposal distribution, so stable procedure can move into weights, deployment-varying contracts stay in context, and enforcement stays in the runtime.

concepts.label: Delivered-prefix serialization
concepts.claim: A training example reconstructs each selected response's input exactly as the model received it, truncations and redactions included, under a recorded tokenizer and template configuration.

concepts.label: Loss masking
concepts.claim: Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.

concepts.label: Loss normalization
concepts.claim: Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.

concepts.label: Exposure bias
concepts.claim: A disagreement rate measured on reference prefixes bounds excess task cost only by min(H, H^2 eps), while the same rate on learner states with bounded recovery cost gives a linear bound, so where imitation error is measured sets the horizon penalty.

concepts.label: Preference training
concepts.claim: When several admissible continuations succeed but differ in cost or risk, DPO over selected spans raises the preferred record's reference-relative score against the dispreferred one from an identical context.

concepts.label: Trajectory distillation
concepts.claim: A costly teacher configuration generates trajectories that pass the same admission as any demonstration, so distillation from sampled tokens is imitation rather than soft-target matching.

concepts.label: Adapter state and modularity
concepts.claim: LoRA cuts trainable parameters but parameter state falls only by the byte ratio of trainable to frozen state, and adapters give modularity, not isolation.

concepts.label: Schema augmentation
