concepts.claim: A corpus with one static tool signature lets the policy memorize argument keys, so augmentation transforms the whole decision context coherently and robustness is measured on held-out schemas.

concepts.label: Packed-example isolation
concepts.claim: Packing is only a memory layout, so block-diagonal attention, per-example label shifts, and position handling must leave each packed example's logits equal to its unpacked logits, a property tested rather than assumed.

concepts.label: Closed-loop release criterion
concepts.claim: Loss values are comparable only under identical split, serialization, mask, and normalization, and promotion requires closed-loop task acceptance under the serving configuration, not lower loss.

concepts.label: Sampled reward contrast
concepts.claim: RLVR scores sampled rollouts with a programmatic check, so the update learns only what the sampler reaches and the reward distinguishes, and a task the policy never solves gives zero signal.

concepts.label: Reward hacking
concepts.claim: Once a check is the objective, any trajectory with proxy reward at least the intended solution's but lower true utility gains weight, and cheap exploits usually have high probability.

concepts.label: Reward as measurement
concepts.claim: The false-accept share of rewarded rollouts moves with the policy's current pass rate rather than being a fixed verifier property, so reward shaping must preserve the priority of correct outcomes.

concepts.label: Credit assignment
concepts.claim: A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.

concepts.label: GRPO coefficients
concepts.claim: GRPO replaces the learned critic with G rollouts per task and broadcasts one standardized coefficient to every sampled token of a rollout, and its clipping and KL estimator choices change how that signal is weighted.

concepts.label: Zero-contrast groups
concepts.claim: A group whose rewards all tie carries no reward gradient, occurring with probability p^G + (1-p)^G, so the rollout cost of one informative group is G/C and difficulty targeting toward p near 0.5 lowers it.

concepts.label: Faithful rollout records
concepts.claim: Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.

concepts.label: Rollout loop sizing
concepts.claim: Agent RL throughput is set by the rollout loop, not the gradient step, so the serial slot cycle caps capacity and Amdahl's law bounds any single-stage speedup.

concepts.label: Entropy collapse
concepts.claim: Symmetric ratio clipping is asymmetric in probability space, so early successes sharpen the policy until groups converge and contrast vanishes, which outcome statistics can diagnose.

concepts.label: Verifier isolation
concepts.claim: Grader isolation placed on the reward path protects the verdict from both the acting policy and the candidate code it submits, so a reward reflects executed tests rather than tampering.

concepts.label: Delegation adds boundaries
concepts.claim: A delegated worker owns a separate child trajectory, and a capable single controller already runs tools and candidates concurrently, so delegation buys only separation of context, authority, and lifecycle, at the price of new boundaries.

concepts.label: Coordination overhead
concepts.claim: Under Speedup(N) = 1/((1-p) + p/N + c(N)) any gain requires c(N) < p(1 - 1/N), the best count sits near sqrt(p/c) for linear overhead, and the serial fraction caps speedup at 1/(1-p).

concepts.label: Three delegation structures
concepts.claim: The dependency graph, the communication topology, and the supervision tree are separate structures, and conflating them hides quadratic communication cost and orphaned lifecycles.

concepts.label: Spawning as admission
concepts.claim: Dynamic spawning makes the execution graph nondeterministic, so the runtime enforces fan-out, concurrency, depth, and deadline bounds and reserves each child's maximum liability before it starts.

concepts.label: Typed envelopes and receipts
concepts.claim: A typed task envelope binds a child to immutable inputs, a scoped grant, a reservation, and required evidence that the runtime resolves, and the receipt carries runtime-populated evidence back, so a worker cannot widen either.

concepts.label: Clean merge is not a valid change
concepts.claim: Shared working directories produce lost updates and torn reads, and write sets collide with probability 1 - exp(-N(N-1)w^2/2F), so isolation is provided per worker and a merge is validated, not trusted.

concepts.label: Correlated reviewers
concepts.claim: Reviewers share each candidate's difficulty, so correlated errors set an irreducible floor on majority-vote false approval that adding reviewers cannot remove.

concepts.label: Matched single-controller baseline
concepts.claim: Delegation is justified only if it beats a capable single controller on the same tasks, criteria, evidence access, concurrency, and resource ceilings, scored on end-to-end acceptance with every initiated task counted.

concepts.label: Subtree cancellation
concepts.claim: Cancellation scope follows delegation lineage and closes admission at each gate, but cancelling a subtree does not settle the obligations its admitted work already created.

concepts.label: Fan-out completion contracts
concepts.claim: An all-results barrier meets a deadline with probability F(t)^N, and a k-of-N rule recovers most of it only when results are interchangeable.

concepts.label: Credit-window flow control
concepts.claim: A credit window enforces free plus outstanding equal to W, bounding in-flight payload and, by Little's law, mean staleness at W/mu, which per-agent token budgets cannot do.

concepts.label: Attenuated delegation
concepts.claim: The runtime assigns each child an identity and a grant contained in its delegator's, sharing permissions but partitioning consumable allowances by atomic reservation.

concepts.label: Slot-pool critical-path bound
concepts.claim: With a fixed slot pool, a dependency graph's completion time is bounded below by both its critical path and its total slot work divided by the slots.

concepts.label: Amdahl's law
concepts.claim: For a fixed amount of work with no coordination overhead, the serial fraction 1-p caps speedup at 1/(1-p) however many workers are added, and the universal scalability law reduces to it when coherency is zero.

concepts.label: Cohort cost per accepted task
concepts.claim: Measured cost per accepted task is the sum of every initiated task's account, each charge in exactly one category, divided by the distinct tasks accepted under one declared contract.

concepts.label: Prefix-cache pricing and compaction payback
concepts.claim: Ideal prefix reuse bills the quadratic re-send at the cached rate, which lowers its coefficient without removing it, so a compaction pays back only after enough turns to recover its rewrite and lost cache.

concepts.label: Critical-path acceleration ceiling
concepts.claim: A speedup g applied to a fraction f of the measured critical path gives T' = T[(1-f) + f/g] and a ceiling of 1/(1-f), which a baseline profile reveals before anything is bought.

concepts.label: Cascade and routing pricing
concepts.claim: A cascade's cost and acceptance are reach-weighted sums, so savings come from the early-exit rate, every reached gate charges whether or not its candidate passes, and fail-through harm is priced in.

concepts.label: Trajectory goodput
concepts.claim: Accepted tasks per unit time is the platform's deliverable, so sustaining goodput G at acceptance alpha requires admitting G/alpha trajectories and any change that lowers acceptance raises offered load.

concepts.label: Queueing cost of utilization
concepts.claim: Near saturation queueing wait grows like rho/(1-rho), so a modest throughput gain from higher utilization costs a multiple in wait that compounds across every serial step of a trajectory.

concepts.label: Budget conservation
concepts.claim: Every budget account in the tree keeps budget = settled + reserved + free under atomic, logged transitions, so a delegation tree conserves spending and a stopped child keeps its reservation until its late bills settle.

concepts.label: Architecture pricing with human fallback
concepts.claim: Deterministic code, a fixed workflow, a bounded loop, and delegation are compared under one acceptance contract by cost per resolved task including human fallback, not by automated cost per automated acceptance.

concepts.label: Dedicated capacity break-even
concepts.claim: Owning capacity beats an API at a delivered utilization u* = F / (3600 R (P_eff - v)), not at a token price.

concepts.label: Speculative decoding profitability
concepts.claim: Speculative decoding pays only when the accepted-draft rate shortens the output-bound critical path by more than draft and verification work add to the bill.

concepts.label: Adaptation payback
concepts.claim: A one-time adaptation investment recovers its cost after N* = C_adapt / (C_base - C_adapted) tasks, never if the per-task saving is nonpositive, and only while acceptance stays equal.

volumes.label: IV
volumes.title: Physical AI
volumes.description: Sensing, planning, and enforcing actions in the world.

concepts.label: Causal boundary
concepts.claim: The causal boundary is the interface where an admitted digital command begins to drive current, force, or flow in the plant; upstream a tensor is a proposal that can be discarded for free, and downstream changing the command costs physical work against inertia over finite time.

concepts.label: Irreversibility and recovery
concepts.claim: Work delivered across the causal boundary has no checkpoint to restore, so recovery is a new constrained motion limited by torque, friction, and drive limits, and the permission path must confirm that a feasible recovery still exists before it admits an action.

concepts.label: Elementary stopping budget
concepts.claim: Stopping distance v*tau_delay + v^2/(2*a_brake) must fit the clear distance, where the delay sums observation age, the unexpired chunk lease, a permission tick, a bus cycle, and brake onset, so every millisecond of latency is travel (1.5 mm per ms at the running machine's 1.5 m/s).

concepts.label: Physical AI scope test
concepts.claim: A system is physical AI only when it has a learned statistical model, consequential physical feedback, and delegated authority at once; an independent deterministic veto does not remove delegated authority, while per-command human approval does.

concepts.label: Digital privileges lost to embodiment
concepts.claim: Moving from advisory prediction through software agency to physical embodiment removes elastic virtual time, transactional rollback, and batchable execution, so data, compute, evaluation, and deployment each acquire physical stakes.

concepts.label: Five-level machine
concepts.claim: The machine is ordered as Brain (learned proposers), Nervous System (buses, schedulers, permission path), Body (plant), Boundary (register writes and sensor captures), and World, with governance as a lifecycle envelope rather than a sixth level, so a failure is diagnosed by the level that failed.

concepts.label: Proposal boundary
concepts.claim: A learned model may only propose; an independent permission path with bounded latency, which the model cannot delay or corrupt, alone admits an action after checking fresh evidence, the stopping envelope, and a feasible fallback, and it acts on its own when the proposer stalls.

concepts.label: Safety convergence at the permission path
concepts.claim: Because physical authority is state-dependent, environmental change, sensor spoofing, and post-incident reconstruction all reduce to three demands on the permission path: fresh authenticated physical state, deterministic authority to intervene with a feasible fallback, and synchronized causal telemetry.

concepts.label: Three machine classes
concepts.claim: Embodied operation divides by the margin it spends (stopping clearance for mass-dominated mobility, force and deformation for contact-dominated manipulation, heat and supply for energy- and thermal-dominated operation), and one task can cross all three.

concepts.label: Crossover speed
concepts.claim: Delay travel equals braking travel at v* = 2*a_brake*tau_delay, so below it latency dominates the stop and above it speed does, and lowering speed shrinks both terms, braking quadratically.

concepts.label: Command-to-motion chain
concepts.claim: A setpoint becomes torque through the position loop, current controller, PWM compare register, inverter, and stator, and the causal boundary sits where that chain first energizes a winding.

concepts.label: Machine card
concepts.claim: The running machine is specified once by a card of registry parameters, each tagged with its evidence category, which later chapters read rather than restate.

concepts.label: Record chain
concepts.claim: Each chapter contributes one machine-checkable record of an assumption with its evidence, producer, consumers, and invalidating conditions, and the chain of records meets at the permission decision.

concepts.label: Five-budget admission
concepts.claim: Before torque reaches a winding the permission path must find non-negative margin in all five physical budgets at once (observation age, stopping distance, deliverable torque, winding temperature, supply), because one budget's slack never pays another's deficit.

concepts.label: Measurement freshness deadline
concepts.claim: An observation's age runs from physical transduction to actuator torque onset and must stay under the freshness deadline E_max / v_max set by the target's speed and the spatial tolerance, with inference only one of many stages.

concepts.label: Velocity ceiling
concepts.claim: The defended stopping distance v*tau + v^2/(2a) + localization and margin allowances must fit the clear distance, solved on the permission path as a clearance-dependent speed ceiling whose credible deceleration is the minimum of independently owned ceilings.

concepts.label: Delivered torque ceiling
concepts.claim: A torque command is a current that winding inductance and voltage headroom pace and the inverter current limit caps, and a drive can clamp current silently while acknowledging packets, so the safety path must read measured current.

concepts.label: Gear ratio trade
concepts.claim: A reduction N multiplies torque by N but reflects rotor inertia by N^2, so acceleration peaks at the inertia-matching ratio and, for a fixed motor and gear, holding heat times reflected inertia does not depend on N.

concepts.label: Thermal duty limits
concepts.claim: Copper loss grows with torque squared, so continuous torque is set by installed heat rejection rather than catalog peak, and a burst spends a stock of heat margin that thermal history has already drawn down.

concepts.label: Shared-rail power integrity
concepts.claim: Compute and drives share one DC bus whose impedance turns a coincident current step into droop toward converter lockout while a regenerative stop pumps energy back, so the permission rail is isolated and held up and every unpowered state is specified.

concepts.label: Limit record
concepts.claim: A physical limit governs an admission decision only as a six-element record (value, conditions, uncertainty, margin, runtime detector, provenance with evidence category), and uncertainty about the measurement is distinct from margin held in reserve.

concepts.label: Reflected rotor inertia
concepts.claim: Rotor inertia appears at the joint output multiplied by the square of the gear ratio, which dominates the effective inertia of a highly geared joint and its impact mass.

concepts.label: Credible deceleration
concepts.claim: The deceleration a stop may assume is the minimum of the brake's capability, the traction limit mu*g, and the drive's torque limit, each owned and evidenced separately.

concepts.label: Virtual spring-damper
concepts.claim: Impedance control makes a joint answer position error with the restoring force of a programmed spring and damper, which bounds contact force through stiffness rather than through position accuracy.

concepts.label: Four boundary events
concepts.claim: Capture, dispatch, admission, and onset are the four timestamped events that divide every capture-to-torque interval into budgetable stages.

concepts.label: Evidence categories
concepts.claim: Every physical value carries one of five evidence categories (measured, derived, datasheet, illustrative, chosen), which decides how far an admission decision may rely on it.

concepts.label: Transmission compliance and backlash
concepts.claim: Gear compliance and backlash put lost motion and limit cycles between motor and load, so measured motor position is not the load's position.

concepts.label: Insulation aging
concepts.claim: Winding insulation ages as an Arrhenius exchange of time at temperature, so the engineering thermal ceiling sits below the insulation class and depends on duty history, not only on peak.

concepts.label: Memory-wall renewal ceiling
concepts.claim: At batch size 1 a proposer streams every weight once per fresh evaluation, so its renewal rate is bounded by sustained bandwidth over weight bytes (14 GB at 142.8 GB/s is 98 ms per sweep, about 10 Hz before vision or decoding).

concepts.label: Prefill-decode split
concepts.claim: One evaluation's prefill reuses each fetched weight across every input token and binds on arithmetic, while each later decode token rereads all weights and binds on bandwidth, so the two halves answer to different hardware limits.

concepts.label: Quantized model is a new model
concepts.claim: Weight-only quantization shortens the bandwidth-bound decode but not the compute-bound prefill, and a quantized checkpoint is a different model whose evaluation evidence must be renewed.

concepts.label: Chunking is a supply lever
concepts.claim: Predicting H setpoints per evaluation divides weight traffic per supplied setpoint by H, but it leaves reaction latency at one renewal period plus one inference, so chunking supplies setpoints without refreshing them.

concepts.label: Two-speed brain
concepts.claim: Because a large backbone's prefill alone exceeds the chunk renewal period, the machine renews motion with a small fast chunk policy beneath a slow intent model rather than waiting for the large model.

concepts.label: Evidence horizon
concepts.claim: Every setpoint in a chunk descends from one capture, so a chunk is valid only while extrapolated target drift stays inside the tolerance margin (about 219 ms for the tracked mug against a 60 ms untracked deadline), and supply and validity are separate budgets.

concepts.label: Checkable proposer interface
concepts.claim: The permission path can refuse only claims it can compare with its own evidence, so an interface that passes a latent vector or a language subtask cannot be grounded or aged, while a geometric payload can.

concepts.label: On-time wrong proposals
concepts.claim: A smooth, in-limit chunk that meets its deadline can still target a nonexistent affordance or carry near-unity confidence far out of distribution, and the proposer cannot report either failure.

concepts.label: Temporal ensembling and real-time chunking
concepts.claim: Exponentially weighted ensembling smooths chunk seams but can blend opposite modes and must drop expired contributions, while real-time chunking freezes the committed prefix and conditions the next chunk on it.

concepts.label: Proposal payload
concepts.claim: A proposal carries its capture times, frame, and geometric content so the permission path can date it and check it against its own evidence.

concepts.label: KV cache footprint
concepts.claim: The key-value cache costs 2*L*d*S*bytes per token of context, so single-observation action models carry none and a long history buys memory traffic, not freshness.

concepts.label: Softmax illusion
concepts.claim: Softmax scores sum to one by construction and saturate far out of distribution, so a confidence score is not calibrated evidence until it is calibrated against held-out outcomes.

concepts.label: Independence requirement
concepts.claim: Under any workload the proposer can generate, the permission path must meet its response bound and keep its authority to refuse, and separate processors are one realization of that requirement, a hypothesis that loaded tests must still confirm.

concepts.label: Rate tiers from time constants
concepts.claim: Each tier takes its rate from a different physical constant (winding L/R and the PWM carrier for the current loop, base travel per tick for the permission tick, weight-sweep cost for the chunk policy, prefill cost for the intent model), not from convenience.

concepts.label: Delay spends phase margin
concepts.claim: Sample-and-hold, compute, and bus transport each subtract omega_c*tau of phase at crossover, so fast loops must close inside the drive and the permission tick can supervise them but never sit in them.

concepts.label: Freshest-proposal mailbox
concepts.claim: Proposals cross rate boundaries as state messages, not events, so a single-slot seqlock or wait-free multi-slot mailbox gives the faster reader one bounded, nonblocking attempt per tick that returns a complete snapshot or keeps the previous one.

concepts.label: Chunk lease
concepts.claim: An admitted chunk may drive the actuators only for a lease counted on the permission path's own clock, derived from the plant: longer than the renewal period plus jitter and short enough to fit under the pre-brake ceiling of the stopping budget.

concepts.label: Authority-expiry timers
concepts.claim: Authority over an admitted chunk ends at the earliest of four independent events (evidence freshness deadline, lease expiry, host heartbeat timeout, protective reflex), and a heartbeat proves only that the host is alive, never that its motion is valid.

concepts.label: Response bound not percentile
concepts.claim: The tick's response time R = C + B + I <= D needs an analytical bound on each term, because a measured maximum or p99 can refute a declared WCET but never establish it.

concepts.label: Sole-writer actuation authority
concepts.claim: The permission path must be the sole writer of every electrical path that can energize a winding, because one unmediated write puts proposer and drives in one failure domain, and the stop itself must be specified in hardware.

concepts.label: Fieldbus occupancy vs response
concepts.claim: Whether every axis exchanges command and feedback within the bus cycle is a necessary check computed from frame geometry, but occupancy alone is not a response bound.

concepts.label: Command interface check burden
concepts.claim: The level at which a proposal enters the drive's position-velocity-current cascade decides what the permission path must verify, from geometry for a position target to integrated motion for a velocity target.

concepts.label: Handoff record and event timing
concepts.claim: Every interface limit is located at one of five handoffs and one of five limits (latency, bandwidth, heat, determinism, fault isolation) and recorded as a handoff record against the capture-to-brake event timing.

concepts.label: Worst-case execution time
concepts.claim: A declared WCET is an analytical upper bound on a task's run time on a given processor, distinct from the unknown true worst case and from any measured maximum.

concepts.label: Safety microcontroller
concepts.claim: A safety microcontroller claims lockstep cores, ECC, memory protection, clock and supply monitors, self-test, and an external windowed watchdog, far more than physical separation on a board.

concepts.label: Setpoint interpolation across rates
concepts.claim: The permission path interpolates admitted waypoints into a setpoint for every bus cycle and falls back on its own when waypoints stop arriving.

concepts.label: Endogenous covariate shift
concepts.claim: Because a physical machine's own executed actions choose its next states and observations, the learner visits a distribution its demonstrations never sampled, so more nominal demonstrations only densify the region the expert already covered.

concepts.label: Compounding error and recoverability
concepts.claim: Behavioral cloning's worst-case excess cost grows as T^2*eps because training error is weighted by the expert's occupancy, and labeling learner-visited states makes it linear only while a recovering action still exists.

concepts.label: Action-label semantics
concepts.claim: One command exists as four signals (requested, mapped, enforced, measured) and every pair must be dated at the exposure midpoint, because the tap chosen and the pairing lag decide what behavior the label teaches.

concepts.label: Demonstration yield and wear
concepts.claim: Physical data is bought in cell time and component life, so less than a quarter of a scheduled hour survives as retained demonstration and failed attempts wear parts like successful ones.

concepts.label: Operational design domain
concepts.claim: The operational design domain is declared before collection, and an archive's coverage is a join between its state-action occupancy and a scenario table derived from that domain, never a property the archive can measure alone.

concepts.label: Intervention curation
concepts.claim: A zero-count cell can mean unvisited, intercepted, cut short by takeover, or censored, and takeover logs are failure-conditioned, so curation locates the divergence point in a pre-trigger buffer and admits only verified recovery.

concepts.label: Embodiment contract
concepts.claim: Every trajectory encodes the sensor geometry, timing, kinematic and torque limits, and compliance of the machine that produced it, so range normalization is cosmetic and borrowed data must pass an embodiment gate.

concepts.label: Provenance record
concepts.claim: Schema-valid arrays can silently encode a shifted camera, a worn pad, a drifted operator, or a mismatched unit, so every archive is bound to an immutable provenance record of plant, calibration, wear, taps, timing, and denominators.

concepts.label: Behavioral cloning
concepts.claim: Behavioral cloning fits actions to observations under the expert's occupancy, so a low held-out loss says nothing about closed-loop competence.

concepts.label: Scenario coverage table
concepts.claim: A scenario table enumerates the cells the declared domain requires over low-dimensional task invariants, because a brute-force state grid is defeated by dimensionality.

concepts.label: Effective sample size of telemetry
concepts.claim: Autocorrelated telemetry carries about N(1-rho)/(1+rho) independent samples, so a higher logger rate cannot populate an unvisited cell.

concepts.label: Causal confusion
concepts.claim: A policy can learn a consequence of the action as its cause (a joint current, a brake light), which is a different failure from contamination by the learner's own actions.

concepts.label: Teleoperation loop latency
concepts.claim: Teleoperation loop latency is display plus human plus command plus mechanics time, dominated by operator reaction, and it leaves step-and-wait artifacts in the labels.

concepts.label: Kinematic topology mismatch
concepts.claim: Cartesian labels recorded on one arm can force a different arm through a singularity or drop a redundant degree of freedom, so action spaces transfer only through the embodiment contract.

concepts.label: Rig-to-rig divergence
concepts.claim: Nominally identical units differ in transmission, mounts, and motor constants, so a failed attempt and a failed recording must be told apart per unit.

concepts.label: Training-regime hidden dependency
concepts.claim: A policy's weights keep what its experience rewarded but not which experience it was, so each regime (demonstrations, logged rewards, simulation, trial on the machine, a pretrained base) leaves a characteristic dependency no training score shows.

concepts.label: Mode averaging
concepts.claim: The squared-error optimum of a point-regression policy is the conditional mean of the action, so two valid evasions average to an action no demonstrator chose, and more data or capacity cannot fix it.

concepts.label: Decoder renewal slack
concepts.claim: A decoder chosen for multimodality must fit the proposal deadline, since latency is encoding plus every dependent decoder evaluation, so the head and evaluation count that training picks decide schedulability.

concepts.label: Offline RL support limit
concepts.claim: Fitting values over a fixed log and acting greedily inflates values at actions the log never executed, and conservative objectives reduce that error but cannot create support the log lacks.

concepts.label: Physical RL exploration cost
concepts.claim: A trial campaign's wall clock is trials times rollout plus reset over rigs (about 93 days of execution for 10^6 latch trials before resets), and every trial spends heat and drivetrain life.

concepts.label: Reality gap as a vector
concepts.claim: Sim-to-real mismatch decomposes into dynamics, sensing, appearance, and timing channels, each sized by paired probing, and randomization covers modeled parameters but never omitted mechanisms.

concepts.label: Update is a new checkpoint
concepts.claim: On-machine fine-tuning absorbs a measurable local mismatch but produces new weights whose earlier evaluations no longer apply, and a gated residual bounds where adaptation may act.

concepts.label: Policy manifest
concepts.claim: The policy manifest records how a checkpoint was produced (regime sequence, base digest, inference contract, data support, omission log, wear log) and computes the declared ODD as support minus omissions.

concepts.label: Reward as specification
concepts.claim: Posing the task as an MDP makes the engineer-written reward and discount the whole objective, so the optimizer exploits any omitted or mismeasured term.

concepts.label: Pretrained borrowed competence
concepts.claim: Post-training a pretrained generalist can cut task-data needs, but no pretraining episode joins this machine's scenario table, so it supplies competence, not evidence.

concepts.label: Simulator contact exploit
concepts.claim: A simulator's contact model decides what the optimizer learns, and a soft penalty spring lets a policy pass through contacts the real plate would resist.

concepts.label: Privileged information limits
concepts.claim: Asymmetric critics and teacher-student distillation speed training under partial observability, but the student cannot recover a state its sensors never observe.

concepts.label: Paired probing
concepts.claim: Identical open-loop excitations on the robot and its simulated twin, scored against error budgets per channel, size each component of the reality gap.

concepts.label: Velocity versus torque drift
concepts.claim: A velocity-commanded policy has a disturbance-rejecting loop beneath it and its error integrates once, while a torque-commanded policy's error integrates twice.

concepts.label: Chunk imitation objective
concepts.claim: Chunked imitation fits a horizon of actions with a Huber penalty on normalized residuals, which buys outlier robustness, not smoothness or feasibility.

concepts.label: RL value functions
concepts.claim: State value, action value, advantage, and the Bellman relation express value as negated cost-to-go, with LQR as the closed-form linear-quadratic case.

concepts.label: Closed-loop estimand
concepts.claim: A physical success rate is the expectation of a frozen outcome predicate over a declared distribution of trial conditions (initial state, environment, unit, frozen policy and permission parameters), so it belongs to that population and to no other.

concepts.label: Outcome channels and censored trials
concepts.claim: Task completion, proposer autonomy, and supervisory burden are separate channels, and an intervened run is an autonomy failure, never a success that was cut short (the censored trial fallacy).

concepts.label: Offline evaluation illusion
concepts.claim: Replay resets the input to the recorded state each step, so a heading bias with a tiny angular MSE can spend a 15 cm aisle clearance in seconds once the loop closes.

concepts.label: Four evidence regimes
concepts.claim: Replay, closed-loop simulation, shadow operation, and constrained physical testing sit on two axes (causal feedback, physical realism) and each trades one distortion for another, so they are not a fidelity ladder.

concepts.label: Predeclared trial protocol
concepts.claim: A finite record supports a claim only if the target ODD, its weights, approximately independent draws, a frozen predicate, and the full denominator are fixed before the first run.

concepts.label: Zero-failure bound
concepts.claim: At zero failures the Wald interval collapses, so a clean record is inverted exactly (failure bound about 3/n), which makes twenty clean runs consistent with a one-in-seven failure rate and makes every added nine cost about ten times the trials.

concepts.label: Exposure wall
concepts.claim: Hazards are rates per operating hour, and bounding a rate lambda with zero events needs about 3/lambda failure-free hours, so rare hazards cannot be demonstrated by sampling the proposer.

concepts.label: Evaluation record
concepts.claim: The evaluation record binds a bounded claim to its target ODD, configuration digests, sampling protocol, complete outcome log, exact statistics, and the catalog of unsupported gaps, which become runtime obligations.

concepts.label: Simulator screening validity
concepts.claim: A simulator earns authority to screen candidates only through a paired sim-and-real benchmark scored for rank inversions, and even then it filters, never certifies.

concepts.label: Sequential and comparative tests
concepts.claim: Early acceptance is valid only under a boundary declared in advance (Wald's SPRT), and comparing two checkpoints needs interleaved, randomized, blinded runs on one unit.

concepts.label: Trajectory confinement
concepts.claim: Shadow operation runs the candidate on the real machine while the baseline keeps authority, so the candidate's inputs stay confined to the baseline's state distribution and its recovery is never tested.

concepts.label: Runtime monitor channels
concepts.claim: Coverage gaps the record cannot close become five runtime monitor channels (input support, latency and freshness, constraint margin, intervention rate, environmental assumption).

concepts.label: Sensor chosen by physical quantity
concepts.claim: Each modality measures one physical quantity (bearing and appearance, metric range, Doppler velocity, contrast change, contact deformation) with its own environmental failures, so sensing is chosen by the quantity the decision needs.

concepts.label: Capture epoch
concepts.claim: A measurement is dated at its exposure midpoint or per-point firing time, never at arrival, and rolling-shutter rows and LiDAR sweeps sample the scene at different instants that capture-time geometry must undo.

concepts.label: Calibration chain
concepts.claim: Every metric claim rests on intrinsics, extrinsics, and inter-sensor time offsets composed along a frame tree at the capture instant, and angular and timing errors scale with range and turn rate.

concepts.label: Observation age
concepts.claim: Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.

concepts.label: Clearance inset from measured residuals
concepts.claim: Spatial error is spent from the same clearance as age, so the clearance inset rests on a measured high quantile of residuals against ground truth, which for stereo grows with range squared.

concepts.label: Metric veto
concepts.claim: Learned depth and semantic confidence are not metric evidence, so a learned head may classify and propose but the range that enters a clearance check comes from qualified metric sensing, which can veto.

concepts.label: Silent versus detectable failure
concepts.claim: Detectable faults raise flags and age out honestly, while silent failures (saturation, contamination, fog backscatter, a misdated frame) deliver valid tensors, so the design must convert silent modes into detectable ones.

concepts.label: Observation contract
concepts.claim: Each observation is wrapped with capture time, clock id, clock-conversion bound, frame, payload, covariance, clearance inset, health bits, and CRC so a consumer can refuse it before reading a payload byte.

concepts.label: Rolling-shutter and de-skew geometry
concepts.claim: Per-row pose interpolation for rolling shutters and per-point de-skew for LiDAR sweeps remove the motion a finite capture interval smears into geometry.

concepts.label: Current evidence age
concepts.claim: The age a consumer computes on its own clock is dispatch age plus the time elapsed since dispatch, and it keeps growing while the observation is reused.

concepts.label: Perception-side independence
concepts.claim: The proposal camera and the admission LiDAR must not share a failure mode, so the metric veto is independent evidence only when its sensing differs from the proposer's.

concepts.label: Latency waterfall
concepts.claim: Sequential capture stages add their durations while overlapped or streamed stages replace the sum, and the waterfall shows which stage spends the age budget.

concepts.label: Environmental degradation
concepts.claim: Fog, rain, glare, and retroreflective vests degrade each modality by its own physics (contrast decay, scattering, blooming, range walk), so a sensor's qualification names its weather.

concepts.label: Input-support monitors
concepts.claim: Out-of-distribution and input-support monitors flag into the health bitmask and can demote a camera to LiDAR-only operation, but they cannot certify what the transducer itself got wrong.

concepts.label: Clock domains and the clock-conversion bound
concepts.claim: Each oscillator stamps time in its own clock domain, so a capture time can be checked only after conversion to the consumer's clock, and that conversion carries a measured bound (offset tail, path asymmetry, drift between syncs) that every age check adds.

concepts.label: Recursive estimation on dated measurements
concepts.claim: A state estimator alternates a prediction that widens uncertainty with elapsed time and updates that narrow it below every input by inverse-variance fusion, applying each measurement at its capture epoch and replaying out-of-sequence ones.

concepts.label: Covariance is a claim
concepts.claim: A filter's reported covariance is a hypothesis tested offline by NEES against ground truth and online by NIS on innovations, and an above-band mean flags the safety-critical overconfident filter.

concepts.label: Occupancy before identity
concepts.claim: Tracking adds identity and velocity for planners, but a tentative track's occupied region must reach clearance consumers before confirmation and stays occupied while it coasts.

concepts.label: Belief record
concepts.claim: Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.

concepts.label: Frames age
concepts.claim: A transform is a belief with its own epoch, so composing a stale camera-to-slot edge with current kinematics yields a pose the arm never occupied, and the lever arm, not clock resolution, sets the error.

concepts.label: Representation follows the query
concepts.claim: The map is chosen by the query it answers inside the permission tick's read budget, so the local snapshot is a dense distance field with four cell states and explicit negative evidence.

concepts.label: Belief expiry
concepts.claim: A belief stops supporting motion when its validated error bound, growing from the evidence epoch, first reaches the task tolerance, and free space erodes inward from the unobserved boundary at a hidden agent's speed bound.

concepts.label: Observability ceiling
concepts.claim: When distinct state histories give identical measurements no estimator can separate them, and innovations stay near zero while the true state drifts, so observability must be designed in by excitation or added sensing.

concepts.label: Out-of-sequence replay
concepts.claim: A ring buffer sized to the delay horizon lets the filter rewind to a late measurement's capture epoch, correct, and replay, and measurements older than the buffer are rejected.

concepts.label: Occlusion and free-space erosion
concepts.claim: Space last seen free stays free only until an unseen agent could have entered it, so occluded free space shrinks at that agent's speed bound and blind crossings need site controls, not memory.

concepts.label: Multi-rate semantic mapping
concepts.claim: A metric loop at camera rate keeps geometry current while foundation backbones update semantics on keyframes, and semantics never certify clearance.

concepts.label: Grounded affordance
concepts.claim: A request names an outcome, not a motion, and a target becomes checkable only as a feature pose in the base frame with approach direction, jaw aperture, and contact-wrench ceiling, each tied to dated sensor evidence.

concepts.label: Goal set is a specification
concepts.claim: The admissible goal set is fixed by the verified task profile from what the grasp can physically absorb, not estimated by the proposer, and the proposal's error envelope plus tracking reserve must fit inside it.

concepts.label: Operators discharged by motion predicates
concepts.claim: A symbolic operator asserts preconditions and effects it cannot verify, so each fact must map to a measurable motion predicate before any step that depends on it is admitted.

concepts.label: Calibrated referent refusal
concepts.claim: A detector score measures prompt match, not uniqueness, so the producer forms a conformal prediction set over referents and refuses with a typed reason unless exactly one candidate remains.

concepts.label: Admission checks physics not meaning
concepts.claim: Metric precision does not establish identity, so a confident wrong object yields a collision-free, torque-limited proposal that passes every check the safety MCU can make, and semantic errors need their own defense.

concepts.label: Expiring intent lease
concepts.claim: The permission side grants a target, never a path, as a lease binding goal set, affordance frame, predicates, ceilings, and an MCU-selected fallback to a hardware deadline at the earliest of the evidence horizon, the administrative lease, and the stopping deadline.

concepts.label: Dynamic reachability
concepts.claim: A target inside the static workspace is still inadmissible if the transit time at the speed ceiling exceeds the remaining evidence window (a handle 300 mm away needs 300 ms against a 219 ms horizon).

concepts.label: Forward occupancy screening
concepts.claim: A corridor is screened early against each tracked person's forward occupancy set, growing from the last measurement at the walking-speed bound, and the screening horizon decides when the planner should stop waiting.

concepts.label: Conformal prediction
concepts.claim: A conformal predictor returns a set of candidate answers whose threshold is calibrated on held-out labeled cases, keeping every candidate it cannot exclude and giving a chosen coverage rate under exchangeability.

concepts.label: Force closure
concepts.claim: A grasp has force closure when its contacts can resist any external wrench within the friction cones, which bounds stability, not the magnitude of the squeeze.

concepts.label: Four handoff invariants
concepts.claim: An intent handoff must keep spatial containment, temporal freshness, dynamic effort, and a certified fallback, and the admission gates check them in cost order.

concepts.label: Task and motion planning
concepts.claim: Task and motion planning certifies symbolic facts with geometric samplers, whether a classical planner or a language model wrote the plan.

concepts.label: Grounding failure modes
concepts.claim: Phantom, stale, ambiguous, misclassified, and dynamically unreachable targets all arrive in the same well-formed wire format, so each needs its own detector.

concepts.label: Trajectory record
concepts.claim: The planner hands over an immutable record naming frame, evidence epoch, seam state, parent intent-lease digest, and four MCU-clock deadlines in two tiers (high-rate chunk lease, hardware commitment cutoff) together with its latched stop.

concepts.label: Replacement latency and handoff tail
concepts.claim: Replacement latency runs from capture to MCU admission (about 115 ms against a 50 ms renewal and a 60 ms lease), so renewal is sustainable only by overlapping requests and every record must carry its own handoff tail.

concepts.label: Manipulator Jacobian
concepts.claim: Clearance and tool limits live in tool space but drives enforce joint limits, so tool-space quantities pass through the configuration-dependent Jacobian, whose weak direction near a singularity demands unbounded joint rates unless damped least squares trades accuracy for bounded rates.

concepts.label: Kinodynamic feasibility
concepts.claim: A collision-free path is executable only if every joint's position, velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque, and current stay within limits along the continuous interpolant, its seams, and its stop, which time parameterization must check.

concepts.label: C2 seam
concepts.claim: Splicing chunks that match only position or velocity leaves an acceleration step that reflected inertia turns into a torque step, so seams must be C2 and the replacement is planned from the projected seam state.

concepts.label: Jerk-limited stopping suffix
concepts.claim: A stop that keeps acceleration continuous must ramp deceleration up and down, so constant-deceleration braking is unexecutable and understates distance, and every admitted trajectory carries a jerk-limited S-curve stop.

concepts.label: Inevitable collision states
concepts.claim: A moving mass enters a state from which every admissible control collides long before contact, so every record names a commitment instant at which its latched stop must begin, and admission closes earlier by the decision-to-onset delay.

concepts.label: Generators are proposers
concepts.claim: Sampling planners, trajectory optimization and MPC, and learned chunks differ in the work they do, not in what they must prove, and a solver's deadline, not its convergence, decides admission.

concepts.label: Future-state conditioning
concepts.claim: Because the arm keeps moving during inference, a replacement is planned from the state projected to the seam and admitted against the measured state.

concepts.label: Model predictive control
concepts.claim: Receding-horizon MPC handles constraints explicitly and gains recursive feasibility only through a terminal invariant set, and its solve time against the period decides whether its output can be admitted.

concepts.label: Time parameterization
concepts.claim: Phase-plane time parameterization finds the fastest timing of a fixed path under velocity, acceleration, and torque bounds, and online generators compute jerk-limited profiles from arbitrary states.

concepts.label: Nonholonomic base planning
concepts.claim: A differential-drive base reaches the same configurations as a holonomic one but through a restricted velocity space, so it plans over controls.

concepts.label: Configuration space
concepts.claim: Planning searches the configuration space and its collision-free subset, and collision queries dominate a sampling planner's run time.

concepts.label: Stopping envelope
concepts.claim: The stopping envelope is the set of states from which the resident stop, after every worst-case delay, halts before the obstacle with localization, protective, and tracking margins intact, and its seven priced rows run as a per-tick speed governor.

concepts.label: Kinetic barrier
concepts.claim: A control barrier function makes its safe set forward invariant only if every admitted input keeps hdot >= -alpha(h), and a barrier on raw distance has relative degree two in torque, so the barrier must carry the cost to stop.

concepts.label: Minimal-intervention filter
concepts.claim: A least-change projection passes a safe proposal untouched and projects a violating one onto the barrier boundary, keeping learned competence, while a structurally invalid proposal is vetoed rather than corrected.

concepts.label: Contact margins
concepts.claim: When contact is the task the kinetic barrier admits only zero speed, so an energy-tank passivity barrier and a separately qualified force channel replace clearance as the margin.

concepts.label: Invariance premises and timing
concepts.claim: A barrier guarantee holds only under model fidelity, bounded disturbance, actuation within a qualified effort error and delay, solver completion inside its budget, and a sample period short enough for inter-sample drift, each watched at runtime.

concepts.label: State-matched fallback ladder
concepts.claim: An arbiter selects directly among project, hold, controlled stop, and torque inhibit by the check that failed and the measured plant state, before the admissible set empties, so one trigger can select different rungs in motion and at standstill.

concepts.label: Certified floor beneath an unrated layer
concepts.claim: The formal protective claim rests on certified drive, scanner, and arm safety functions beneath the permission path, which is an unrated performance layer, with only the lease and heartbeat watchdog selected for a rating.

concepts.label: Enforcement record
concepts.claim: The enforcement record joins a signed enforcement contract (tracking bound, barrier coefficients, deadlines, effort-error bounds, routing) to a per-tick admitted command with its margin, detector, and rung.

concepts.label: Recoverable set
concepts.claim: The stopping envelope is the machine's recoverable set, the states from which the resident stop still succeeds, and the viable set and barrier safe set are drawings of it.

concepts.label: Tracking bound
concepts.claim: The feedback tracker guarantees a worst-case tracking tube only inside its qualified envelope, so the enforcer insets every clearance by it and watches the premises that keep it true.

concepts.label: Net braking authority
concepts.claim: Available deceleration is net of gravity and bias in the worst direction, and integrator unwinding and saturation spend it before the stop begins.

concepts.label: Speed and separation monitoring
concepts.claim: Speed and separation monitoring keeps a protective separation distance (the person's travel, the robot's reaction and stopping travel, intrusion distance, and position uncertainties) between a moving arm and a person as a certified function.

concepts.label: Human separation distance
concepts.claim: The pedestrian intrusion distance v_h(tau + T_stop) sets how much clearance a walking person consumes during the stop, which bounds the walking-person speed ceiling.

concepts.label: Functional-safety integrity grading
concepts.claim: Safety functions, not components, are graded by SIL or by a Performance Level that combines category, MTTFd, diagnostic coverage, and common-cause defenses; the standards set the required level for each function of this machine, and only the functions selected for a rating carry the formal claim.

concepts.label: Passive-compliance stiffness
concepts.claim: A series compliance, whose stiffness falls below that of its softer element because compliances add, slows the force rise and bounds impact force passively when the enforcer cannot stop in time, so its stiffness is part of the contact margin.

concepts.label: Per-resource independence inventory
concepts.claim: A separate core or chip is not independent by construction, because memory protection governs where a transaction may go, not when it is served, so independence is argued row by row over every shared resource, including supply, clock, and reset.

concepts.label: Memory contention and miss handling
concepts.claim: Memory arbiters schedule bursts, not averages, so a safety read waits on the backlog ahead of it and the controller's policy, and shared-cache miss handling, not bandwidth, threatens the declared bound.

concepts.label: Thermal throttling hangover
concepts.claim: On a shared die sustained inference drives the junction past the trip point, the governor cuts the clock so every tick overruns its bound, and hysteresis holds the clock down for seconds after the burst ends.

concepts.label: Declared WCET as falsification threshold
concepts.claim: Loaded execution is isolated execution plus shared-hardware interference, and the placement claims that interference is zero, so any loaded tick above the declared WCET refutes the placement's timing premise even when it still meets the deadline.

concepts.label: Boundary contract and windowed watchdog
concepts.claim: The exchange has two separately timed obligations (board-link transport, then one bounded local publication read inside the WCET), and liveness needs a windowed watchdog that catches early feeds as well as late ones.

concepts.label: Priced remediation ladder
concepts.claim: A refuted placement forces a remedy matched to the coupling (static reservation, spatial partitioning, separate silicon), each paid in a different currency and leaving a named residual.

concepts.label: Dispatch-to-admission allocation
concepts.claim: The selected placement must allocate the interval from perception dispatch to admission (residual inference, serialization, validation, activation, up to one tick) and fit it under the stopping spare.

concepts.label: Placement record
concepts.claim: The placement record binds the declared WCET and deadline to the execution domain, privilege, period, unloaded and loaded maxima, bus QoS, droop and thermal limits, mitigations, and the conditions left untested.

concepts.label: Supply, clock, and reset domains
concepts.claim: Privilege checks govern digital access while the shared rail powers the gates that perform them, so droop, clock faults, and shared resets are failure domains beneath privilege.

concepts.label: Offload timing screen
concepts.claim: An off-board result counts only if its tail network time plus remote processing fits the transaction window and the full dispatch-to-admission ceiling, so wireless tails disqualify offload for anything that renews the lease.

concepts.label: Mixed-criticality scheduling
concepts.claim: Execution budgets depend on the assurance level, so when a high-criticality task exhausts its lower budget the scheduler withdraws service from low-criticality work to keep the enforcer's tick.

concepts.label: Static-partitioning hypervisor
concepts.claim: A static-partitioning hypervisor binds cores, memory, and peripherals to isolated partitions at boot and colors caches, the standard pattern for a real-time enclave on a shared die.

concepts.label: WCET analysis families
concepts.claim: WCET comes from static analysis, measurement plus margin, hybrid methods, or probabilistic tail models, and local worst cases do not compose to a global one on modern microarchitectures.

concepts.label: Coupling-timescale ladder
concepts.claim: Couplings act on different timescales (nanosecond droop, microsecond queueing, millisecond ticks, second-scale throttling, hour-scale chassis heat), which tells a rail-correlated fault from a temperature-correlated one.

concepts.label: Intervention transfers the right to propose
concepts.claim: Supervisory intervention transfers the right to propose on named actuator channels from the policy to an authenticated person, committed on a control tick and bounded by a lease, while every human command still passes the permission check.

concepts.label: Takeover delay in the stopping budget
concepts.claim: Takeover latency (sensory, cognitive, motor, console) is long-tailed and must be budgeted at a design percentile as a delay before braking, which sets the speed a supervised machine may run.

concepts.label: Clearance-derived fallback deadline
concepts.claim: Fixing the current speed and solving the stopping inequality for the wait gives the latest fallback deadline, so a handover timeout is a function of state, and any configured ceiling is clipped to it.

concepts.label: Authority leases and physical presence
concepts.claim: Autonomous chunks and manual sessions hold separate leases on the safety MCU's clock, so a silent policy, a dropped link, or an incapacitated operator loses authority to a state-matched local fallback.

concepts.label: Single-writer handover handshake
concepts.claim: Per channel, authority resolves every tick to exactly one state with the enforcer the sole actuator writer, and a four-phase request-acknowledge-commit-release handshake moves it.

concepts.label: Bumpless transfer
concepts.claim: A setpoint swap at commit demands an unbounded command derivative, so the enforcer blends between latched endpoints with a quintic smoothstep whose duration is set by the rate limit and paid from stopping reserve.

concepts.label: Mode confusion and per-channel annunciation
concepts.claim: Single-writer gating resolves arbitration faults but not mode confusion, the gap between the mode a supervisor believes and the actual one, which only per-channel masks and annunciation fix.

concepts.label: Authority record
concepts.claim: The authority record binds a sealed static authority manifest to a per-tick evidence tuple of time, authority state, measured state, proposed and admitted commands, so every handover is reconstructable and attributable.

concepts.label: Authenticating interventions
concepts.claim: Protective stops never wait for verification while motion commands, which inject energy, must be authenticated, attributable, and fresh, and the verifier's availability must itself be protected.

concepts.label: Causal intervention masking
concepts.claim: A takeover log is split into intervals by commit, blend-end, and stabilization timestamps, and only the stabilized human interval trains as demonstration.

concepts.label: Trustworthy operational logs
concepts.claim: Reconstruction needs a log that survives physical failure and records both sides of the causal boundary on synchronized clocks, because dispatched commands alone cannot prove delivered torque.

concepts.label: Ironies of automation
concepts.claim: Automation leaves the human the hardest, least-time cases with degraded skill and a stale forward model, so oversight degrades exactly when it is needed.

concepts.label: Shared autonomy blending
concepts.claim: Blending human and policy commands works only when goals are unimodal and every intermediate blend is admissible; across modes a convex combination is a new, unchecked command.

concepts.label: Remote-assistance session admission
concepts.claim: A remote assistant is admitted only if reaction budget, handshake latency, manual lease, and blend window fit the remaining clearance, and remote assistance is never a safety layer.

concepts.label: Operating envelope and coupled corners
concepts.claim: A protective claim holds only over a declared operating envelope that couples the external ODD with internal execution state (load, bus voltage, saturation, temperature), and its danger lives at the coupled corners, not the nominal center.

concepts.label: Precommitted oracle
concepts.claim: A fault trial counts as evidence only against an oracle fixed before the run that returns signed margins, scored from the event the fault disrupts rather than from the start of the trial.

concepts.label: Fault-list derivation
concepts.claim: Faults come from inverting each recorded design guarantee at its handoff and from working forward from the physical machine, each built as a five-element chain from cause to violated claim.

concepts.label: Transduction and proposer attacks
concepts.claim: A transduction attack delivers a checksum-valid packet whose measurement is false, so packet integrity is never an oracle for perception, and a wrong action inside the envelope after prompt injection or a patch is a coverage deficit, never a pass.

concepts.label: Qualification ladder
concepts.claim: Software-, processor-, and hardware-in-the-loop rigs and the physical fault rig each make a different part of the loop real while throughput falls by orders of magnitude, so a mechanism can fail only on a rung that contains it.

concepts.label: Falsification by signed robustness
concepts.claim: Signed temporal-logic robustness turns testing into an optimization that searches for the smallest margin, and a simulated margin counts only after its sim-to-real transfer discount.

concepts.label: Rare-event rates and tails
concepts.claim: Failure probability cannot be read from falsification runs or naive Monte Carlo, so rates need importance sampling with a tuned proposal and tail magnitudes need weighted extreme value fits.

concepts.label: Fault-record set
concepts.claim: Each fault record binds a signed header (trial, claim, envelope point, injection, oracle digest, latencies, margins, verdict) to the independently retained trace, carrying evidence and its gaps to release.

concepts.label: Four verdicts and independent witnesses
concepts.claim: Every trial returns pass, fail, invalid, or unobservable, unmeasured fields are recorded as unavailable rather than zero, and an independent witness keeps a pass from resting on the system under test.

concepts.label: Extreme value theory
concepts.claim: Extreme value theory fits the distribution of block maxima or threshold exceedances, so a tail estimate needs many independent extremes and a justified tail family.

concepts.label: Importance-sampling weight diagnostic
concepts.claim: Kish's effective sample size of the importance weights and a tail-coverage check reveal when a few heavy weights carry the estimate.

concepts.label: Digital twin delusion
concepts.claim: A simulator never compared with a measured stop of this machine is a model, not a twin, and earns no evidential weight.

concepts.label: Probe effect
concepts.claim: Timing the enforcer with on-target logging changes its timing, so verification uses non-intrusive hardware trace.

concepts.label: Safety case
concepts.claim: Release adjudicates physical inequalities (stop inside the clear distance, contact force under the assessed limit, WCET inside its deadline) through a claim-argument-evidence case whose warrants say why each piece of evidence supports its claim.

concepts.label: Conjunctive premises and diverse legs
concepts.claim: When every child claim is required the case is conjunctive and its confidence falls below every premise, so an assessor looks for the least-supported premise, and only genuinely independent sufficient legs add confidence.

concepts.label: Three signed verdicts
concepts.claim: The argument resolves into a signed verdict loaded as the machine's operating permit (UNCOND for the assessed envelope, COND for a separately evidenced restricted limit set, REFUSE naming the next measurement).

concepts.label: Standing conditions
concepts.claim: A verdict lives only while its premises hold, so each premise is bound to a detector or site procedure at a cadence set by its degradation mechanism, and an unknown premise refuses like a breach.

concepts.label: Release manifest
concepts.claim: The release manifest binds every upstream record, the argument digest, binary hashes, calibration, standing conditions, wear budget, expiry, and the adjudicator's signature to one configuration and gates motion fail-closed.

concepts.label: Updates reopen claims
concepts.claim: An update reopens the claims whose evidence it touches, an unchanged enforcer binary does not imply an unchanged containment argument, and shadow mode filters candidates while contained canaries qualify them.

concepts.label: Certification authorizes a configuration
concepts.claim: Certification follows the machinery route (risk reduction, rated functions, drive stops, mobile-manipulator standards) and authorizes a configuration with its evidence, not a capability.

concepts.label: Adversarial review and defeaters
concepts.claim: Before signing, an independent reviewer hunts defeaters with probes at the envelope extremes, domain transfer, structural independence, and unmonitored wear, and the review recurs against normalization of deviance.

concepts.label: Fleet evidence one outcome at a time
concepts.claim: Fleet exposure narrows intervals for common outcomes but leaves rare severe outcomes wide, so each outcome's claim is licensed separately and disclosed.

concepts.label: Shadow mode deployment
concepts.claim: Shadow mode runs a release candidate beside the incumbent with no actuator authority, logging divergence as action and barrier-rate discrepancies, which filters candidates but cannot qualify them.

concepts.label: Canary non-inferiority
concepts.claim: A contained canary qualifies an update by a non-inferiority test on the intervention-rate ratio against a margin declared in advance, with sequential stopping.

concepts.label: Approval record
concepts.claim: The approval record names, for each decision behind an admitted action, the person who approved it and answers for it, together with the human roles, permit stage, exposed groups, records about people, and shifted labor, and the release gate reads it as a standing condition so that a decision with no named owner refuses operation the way an unknown premise does.

concepts.label: Decisions behind an admitted action
concepts.claim: One admitted command rests on decisions made earlier by different parties (policy, enforcer, authority state, envelope, crossing rule, staffing), so each party can point to another, most of those decisions never appear in a runtime log, and a chain of k separately kept links is complete only with the product of their probabilities, so the links must be recorded on purpose.

concepts.label: Oversight a person can perform
concepts.claim: A human role counts as a countermeasure only if its holder has the time, information, and authority to act within the time the hazard leaves, including the queue one person serves, and a role that fails any of the three moves blame onto that person without adding protection.

concepts.label: Staged permission
concepts.claim: Permission to operate is granted in stages (testing with a safety driver or spotter, driverless or unattended testing, open deployment), each for a named configuration, domain, evidence, and reporting duties, left on evidence gathered at that stage and withdrawn for a configuration change, an incident, or a withheld record.

concepts.label: Detection gaps become stopping gaps
concepts.claim: A group of people a detector sees less often needs more frames before detection can be relied on, so a stop sized for the best-detected group loses distance before braking and strikes the other group with speed and energy that follow from the distance lost, and each group's sample must be large enough for its interval to resolve the gap.

concepts.label: Recorded people
concepts.claim: Records that reconstruct an admitted action also record operators, bystanders, demonstrators, and coworkers, so each identifying record declares its purpose, retention period, what is removed before storage, and its readers, and an access and retention audit enforces the declaration as a standing condition.

concepts.label: Worker burden
concepts.claim: Automation moves a task's labor into rescue, sweeping, monitoring, and data collection, and creates records that could be used to score workers, so a deployment counts the labor it moves and bars uses of its safety records that were never declared.

concepts.label: Unconsented risk
concepts.claim: The people a machine puts at risk are often not the people who chose it, so an aggregate risk figure can improve while risk concentrates on them, and exposure is reported per group and per location with whether each group chose it.

concepts.label: Legible intent
concepts.claim: People protect themselves by predicting where a machine will go, so motion that reveals its goal early and explicit signals let them yield sooner, and signals are shown only where measured detection supports the trust they invite.

concepts.label: Incident disclosure duty
concepts.claim: An operating permit carries a duty to report incidents completely and on time, so a permit can be withdrawn for a withheld or incomplete record as well as for the motion it describes.

concepts.label: Four-law audit of a new machine
concepts.claim: The method transfers to an unfamiliar machine as four ordered questions (what the task cannot undo and which measured bound excludes it, whether closed-loop evidence covers the enforced envelope, which independent path admits each proposal, and what evidence bounds the authority granted), not as the warehouse machine's numbers.

concepts.label: Residual-claims register
concepts.claim: A premise no onboard sensor reports is not the envelope's monitored unknown, so it is bound to a standing restriction, an accountable owner, and a predeclared closure test, chosen among responses (probe, restrict, add sensing, accept by judgment) by the claim each can support.

concepts.label: Next capability by missing evidence
concepts.claim: Open register entries fall into classes by the evidence they lack (an unmeasured observable, an evaluation deficit, a theoretical deficit) or by a scope mismatch that no evidence inside the present architecture repairs, and the class, not the urgency, selects the next experiment, with each restriction priced against the campaign that would retire it.

concepts.label: Observational indistinguishability
concepts.claim: When two states that need different responses produce identical observations until the action deadline, no model on that channel can separate them, and the latest useful observation is set by braking distance over speed.

concepts.label: Shield dilution
concepts.claim: A shield's per-command guarantee becomes a hazard-rate claim only conditionally, lambda_sys <= lambda_h(1 - c) + lambda_cc, and observed fleet rates already include the shield, so multiplying them by an interception factor double-counts.
